1402	### 2.3 `NativeContextV2` (Rust)
1403	
1404	**There is exactly one native-context record and one `H` domain per language.**
1405	`NativeContextV2` is the **Rust** context; `TypeScriptNativeContextV2` (§2.4) is the
1406	TypeScript one. Neither is a general "native context": a universe binds the record of its
1407	own language and refuses the other.
1408	
1409	Descriptor (domain `native.context.rust.v2`): `{schemaVersion:2, targetTriple,
1410	hostTriple, toolchain: ToolchainIdentityV1, toolClosure: ToolClosureV1, baseCfg,
1411	resolverVersion, dependencySourceSetId, unifiedFeaturesId, preparedOutputSetId|null,
1412	configProjection: CargoConfigProjectionV2}`.
1413	
1414	`rustcDevLlvmDigest` is at **`NativeContextV2.toolchain.rustcDevLlvmDigest`**, inside
1415	`ToolchainIdentityV1` — not a top-level field of the context (a citation that says only "in
1416	native-context schema 2" is reachable but under-specified). Its value is the 64-hex suffix
1417	of the `closure2` identity of the admitted `kind=rust-dev-llvm` closure, so `"closure2:" +`
1418	the field must name a retained closure of that kind whose recomputed identity equals it;
1419	`admit_native_context('rust', …)` performs exactly that join against the retained closure
1420	descriptor and tree.
1421	
1422	`ToolClosureV1` = `{rustc, cargo, linker|null, ar|null, procMacroServer, closureId}`
1423	— the raw digests of every executable the adapter may select, all members of the
1424	signed `closure2` named by `closureId`. **Every tool that runs is in this
1425	closure**: `rustc`, `cargo`, the linker rustc spawns when a build script or
1426	proc-macro crate is linked, `ar`, and the proc-macro server. No `PATH` lookup, no
1427	system `cc`, no `RUSTC`/`CARGO`/`RUSTUP_*`/`CARGO_HOME` from the environment. If a
1428	platform family has no bundled linker in the closure, in-host preparation is
1429	`UNSUPPORTED-TYPED` there (`native.execution-not-authorized`, cause
1430	`linker-unavailable`); it never falls back to a system linker.
1431	
1432	The host resolved-inputs adapter computes the context before PlanId; the worker
1433	recomputes it after sealed inputs are received and refuses with
1434	`Unavailable(native-context-mismatch)` before Analyze if any byte differs (§9.5).

1436	### 2.4 `TypeScriptNativeContextV2` (TypeScript/JavaScript)
1437	
1438	Descriptor (domain `native.context.typescript.v2`): `{schemaVersion:2, languageMode,
1439	toolchain: TypeScriptToolchainIdentityV1, toolClosure: TypeScriptToolClosureV1,
1440	configProjection: TypeScriptConfigProjectionV2, moduleResolutionMode, packageModuleType,
1441	nodeModulesLayoutDigest|null, lockfileIdentity|null}`.
1442	
1443	`TypeScriptToolchainIdentityV1` = `{compilerName:"typescript", compilerVersion,
1444	compilerPackageDigest, typescriptStdlibMerkleRoot, standardLibraryComponentDigests[],
1445	libSelection[]}`. `TypeScriptToolClosureV1` = `{compiler, runtime, closureId}`.
1446	
1447	**Exact field locations and producing recipe.** Every value is computed by the host
1448	resolved-inputs adapter before PlanId from **admitted, retained** bytes; none is read from a
1449	worker claim, a `tsc --version` string or the environment.
1450	
1451	| Field | Produced from |
1452	|---|---|
1453	| `toolchain.compilerVersion` | the `semanticVersion` of the **admitted signed compiler closure manifest** named by `toolClosure.closureId`; admission refuses when the two differ, so a version string and the bytes it labels cannot drift apart |
1454	| `toolchain.compilerPackageDigest` | a member digest of that retained `kind=toolchain` closure tree |
1455	| `toolchain.typescriptStdlibMerkleRoot` | identity §3's existing recipe: the **64-hex suffix** of the `closure2` identity of the admitted `kind=stdlib` closure. `"closure2:" +` the value must name a retained closure of that kind whose recomputed identity equals it |
1456	| `toolchain.standardLibraryComponentDigests` | the **complete** declaration-file inventory of that retained stdlib tree — one row per `.d.ts` member, selected or not, `component` = the member basename, sorted by `component`. A missing row refuses `native.native-context-stdlib-inventory-incomplete:<name>`, because an alternate partial declaration inventory for the same retained library is not the required complete record. A tree in which two paths share a basename refuses `native.native-context-stdlib-tree-ambiguous-basename:<name>` rather than resolving the join arbitrarily |
1457	| `toolchain.libSelection` | the effective `lib` **names** the resolved `compilerOptions` select after `target` defaulting, sorted; each must map to a retained component under the published name-to-component join below. These are `lib` names (`es2022`), never declaration-file names |
1458	| `toolClosure.compiler`, `toolClosure.runtime` | raw digests of the bundled compiler and of the bundled JavaScript runtime that executes it, both members of the signed closure named by `closureId`. No `PATH` lookup, no system `node`, no `NODE_OPTIONS`/`NODE_PATH`/`TS_NODE_*` from the environment |
1459	| `configProjection.honoredOptions` | the closed subset of the **effective** resolved `compilerOptions` (or of `SynthesizedCompilerOptionsV1` under `js-synthesized`) that changes program membership, module resolution or checking |
1460	| `configProjection.strippedOptions` | every option removed, with a typed reason (`selects-an-executable`, `emits-output`, `reads-the-environment`, `acquires-types-from-the-network`, `not-a-resolution-or-membership-option`). Stripping is disclosed here and is never a reason to read the option from anywhere else. `typeAcquisitionEnabled` and `executableSelected` are schema constants `false` |
1461	| `configProjection.configGraphPaths` | every `tsconfig`/`jsconfig` file of the resolved `extends` graph, in the snapshot, sorted by logical path; empty under `configOrigin=synthesized` |
1462	| `nodeModulesLayoutDigest` | raw SHA-256 of `C(ResolvedNodeModulesLayoutV1)` — the retained resolution read-set layout — or `null` exactly when `nodeModulesInReadSet=false` |
1463	| `lockfileIdentity` | `{kind, path, contentSha256}` of the admitted lockfile, or `null` when `lockfileKind=none` |
1464	
1465	**Retained trees.** The stdlib closure and the compiler closure are retained **whole** —
1466	complete foundation `closure` descriptor and complete file tree — and joined to the selected
1467	compiler. `admit_native_context` recomputes each closure identity from its retained record
1468	and refuses `native.native-context-closure-unretained`,
1469	`native.native-context-closure-identity-mismatch` or
1470	`native.native-context-closure-kind-mismatch` before any digest comparison. The stdlib merkle
1471	root is therefore never a bare number a caller can assert.
1472	
1473	**`libSelection` → `standardLibraryComponentDigests`: the published join.** The
1474	two arrays hold different vocabularies on purpose and neither is rewritten into
1475	the other. `libSelection` holds effective **`lib` names** — the values
1476	`configProjection.honoredOptions.lib` carries (`es2022`, `dom`), which is why the
1477	two are compared directly. `standardLibraryComponentDigests[].component` holds
1478	**declaration-file basenames** of the retained stdlib closure tree
1479	(`lib.es2022.d.ts`). Because the join between them is enforced at context
1480	admission with its own typed refusal, it is published here rather than left to
1481	ecosystem convention; two hosts inventing different mappings would admit and
1482	refuse the *same* retained context bytes differently, which is a public admission
1483	divergence, not implementation freedom.
1484	
1485	| Rule | Statement |
1486	|---|---|
1487	| Fold | `fold(n)` is Unicode **Default Case Conversion `toLowercase(X)`**: the **full**, **non-tailored**, **context-sensitive** default lowercase mapping (Unicode Standard §3.13 / UAX #21). It is the **same single fold** the honored-`lib` agreement below uses, and this section defines no other: no NFC/NFKC step, no trimming, no alias table, no prefix or suffix matching. Reference implementation `native_evidence_model.v2.lib_name_fold` |
1488	| Mapping | `component(n) = "lib." + fold(n) + ".d.ts"`. Total, deterministic and **one-directional**: a selected name maps to exactly one component basename, and a component is never mapped back into a selected name |
1489	| Membership | for every `n` in `libSelection`, `component(n)` must be an element of the declared `component` set. A name whose component is absent refuses `native.native-context-lib-not-retained:<n>` — §10 route `request-rejected` (2) / `REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED`, before PlanId |
1490	| Equality | `{fold(n) : n ∈ libSelection}` must equal `{fold(m) : m ∈ honoredOptions.lib}`. `honoredOptions.lib` is required and non-empty in the closed resolved context, so this agreement always applies and is **not** weakened by the mapping. Two `libSelection` entries with the same fold refuse `native.native-context-field-mismatch:duplicate-lib-selection`; a set disagreement refuses `native.native-context-field-mismatch:libSelection` |
1491	| Order | `libSelection` is sorted by the raw UTF-8 bytes of the **retained, unfolded** names; `standardLibraryComponentDigests` by the raw UTF-8 bytes of `component`. Each record keeps its own specified order for hashing — folding is a comparison, never a rewrite of a retained value, and neither array is re-spelled into the other's vocabulary |
1492	
1493	**What `fold` is, and what it is not.** The three plausible operations are genuinely different
1494	and only one of them is the one this admission performs, so it is named rather than approximated.
1495	
1496	| Discriminator | `fold` (**full default lowercase**) | simple lowercase | case folding |
1497	|---|---|---|---|
1498	| `U+0130` LATIN CAPITAL LETTER I WITH DOT ABOVE | `U+0069 U+0307` — **two** code points, through `SpecialCasing.txt` | `U+0069`, one code point | `U+0069 U+0307` |
1499	| `U+039F U+03A3` (sigma in **final** position) | `U+03BF U+03C2` — the `Final_Sigma` condition | `U+03BF U+03C3` | `U+03BF U+03C3` |
1500	| `U+03A3 U+039F` (sigma **not** final) | `U+03C3 U+03BF` | `U+03C3 U+03BF` | `U+03C3 U+03BF` |
1501	| `U+00DF` LATIN SMALL LETTER SHARP S | `U+00DF` — unchanged | `U+00DF` | `U+0073 U+0073` |
1502	
1503	So `fold` is **not** `Simple_Lowercase_Mapping` (it expands, and it is position-dependent) and
1504	**not** `Case_Folding` (sharp s is unchanged). It is **non-tailored** — the root locale, with no
1505	Turkish/Azeri dotless-i and no Lithuanian tailoring — so the result must never depend on an ambient
1506	locale, an environment variable or a host language setting.
1507	
1508	**Version custody, and the portability consequence it does not hide.** The result of a default case
1509	conversion is determined by the Unicode case data the host carries, so `fold` is deterministic
1510	**given a case-data version**, and this design binds the reference derivation to one:
1511	`native_evidence_model.v2.UNICODE_CASE_DATA_VERSION`, currently **UCD 15.0.0**, the version the
1512	table above was measured against. Two hosts on different case data can fold the same name
1513	differently — for a code point unassigned in one of them (an unassigned code point folds to itself),
1514	or for one whose mapping changed between the versions — and because `libSelection` enters the
1515	context descriptor and therefore `PlanId`, that would be an admission divergence, not a cosmetic
1516	one. This contract does **not** claim the fold is invariant across every runtime. It requires the
1517	version to be a declared, checkable property rather than whatever the runtime happens to ship:
1518	`unicode_case_data_agreement()` reports the running version against the declared one so drift is
1519	disclosed instead of silently changing an outcome. Nothing here narrows the field to ASCII to
1520	sidestep the question — it is simply true that every `lib` name in the pinned compiler's own option
1521	vocabulary is ASCII, where all three operations above coincide, and that is a fact about the current
1522	vocabulary rather than a constraint on the value.
1523	
1524	**Custody: the two arrays answer different questions.** `libSelection` is the
1525	*configuration-facing* record of what the resolved options selected, and it is
1526	what the universe/config agreement is checked against.
1527	`standardLibraryComponentDigests` is the *tree-facing* **complete** declaration
1528	inventory of the retained stdlib closure — one row per `.d.ts` member with its
1529	raw digest, selected or not. So the selection never narrows the inventory and the
1530	inventory never adds a selected name: a missing inventory row refuses
1531	`native.native-context-stdlib-inventory-incomplete:<basename>`, and a tree in
1532	which two paths share a basename refuses
1533	`native.native-context-stdlib-tree-ambiguous-basename:<basename>` — the mapping's
1534	target would not be unique, and an arbitrary resolution is exactly what this
1535	refusal exists to prevent. The join reads **no other input**: not a
1536	caller-supplied map, not a filesystem lookup, not a compiler query, not the
1537	`typescriptStdlibMerkleRoot` value on its own.
1538	
1539	**No platform *field*, and the identity is still platform-specific.** Unlike the Rust context there

1540	is no `targetTriple`/`hostTriple`, because TypeScript *resolution semantics* — which specifiers
1541	resolve, which subjects are examined, what is checked — are platform-invariant by design (§1.1).
1542	That is a design selection of this contract, not a measurement, and it is **not** a claim that the
1543	identity is platform-invariant: `toolClosure.closureId` names a signed closure whose foundation
1544	`closure` descriptor includes `platform`, so the same source analysed with the platform-specific
1545	executables of two families mints two `nativeContextId`s — as it must, because different bytes ran
1546	(`typescript-context-identity-is-platform-specific-through-its-signed-tool-closure`).
1547	
1548	**Universe and Plan binding.** `typescript-v2.nativeContextId` is
1549	`H("native.context.typescript.v2", descriptor)` in the `Sha256Text` form. `PlanId` binds the
1550	same digest through `plan.nativeContextDigests`, which takes the **bare 64 hex** (§11, the
1551	foundation `plan` record's spelling) and is a canonical **set**: several units of one language
1552	legitimately share one context, and identical admitted contexts collapse to one member — that is
1553	deduplication of an identical descriptor, never of two different ones.
1554	
1555	`bind_typescript_universe(universe, admission, context)` refuses a universe whose `nativeContextId`
1556	this host did not mint (`native.universe-context-binding-mismatch`) and refuses a Rust-minted context
1557	outright (`native.native-context-language-mismatch`). The **retained context bytes are a required
1558	argument**: there is no context-free admit path, because an optional field-agreement check is not a
1559	rule — a caller that omitted it would obtain exactly the bypass this join exists to close. Omission
1560	is the typed refusal `native.universe-context-not-supplied`
1561	(`typescript-universe-bound-without-the-retained-context-refuses`); context bytes that do not hash to
1562	the admitted id refuse
1563	`native.universe-context-binding-mismatch:context-bytes-are-not-the-admitted-ones`.
1564	
1565	Given those bytes the two records must **agree where they overlap**: a matching `nativeContextId`
1566	commits to the context bytes, not to the universe's copy of them, so `languageMode`,
1567	`packageModuleType`, `allowJs`, `checkJs`, `lockfileKind`, `nodeModulesInReadSet`,
1568	`jsDiagnosticsEnabled`, `jsAdmittedToProgram`, `configOrigin`, the `extends`-graph emptiness and the
1569	synthesized-options presence are each checked against the context and refuse
1570	`native.universe-context-field-mismatch:<field>`.
1571	
1572	The context itself also has mandatory agreement rules. `moduleResolutionMode`
1573	equals `configProjection.honoredOptions.moduleResolution`. `libSelection` is
1574	strictly sorted by UTF-8 name bytes, contains no duplicate names under the
1575	published `fold`, and selects the same folded name set as the honored `lib` list
1576	— the same `fold` the component join above uses, and the only one this section
1577	defines; each record retains its specified order for hashing. The closed resolved context
1578	always materializes that nonempty list. When source configuration omits `lib`,
1579	the resolver supplies the pinned compiler's target-default library selection

1618	## 3. Sealed dependency inputs (AR-07)
1619	
1620	### 3.1 `DependencySourceSetV1`
1621	
1622	Identity domain `native.dependency-source-set.v1`. Closed descriptor:
1623	`{schemaVersion:1, language:"rust", lockfileIdentity, packages:
1624	[DependencyPackageSourceV1…] sorted by (name, version, sourceId) UTF-8 bytes,
1625	completeness:{state, missing[]}}`.
1626	
1627	`DependencyPackageSourceV1`:
1628	
1629	| Field | Rule |
1630	|---|---|
1631	| `name`, `version` | exact `[[package]]` values from `Cargo.lock` |
1632	| `sourceKind` | `registry \| git \| path \| vendored` |
1633	| `sourceId` | exact `source` string from `Cargo.lock`, or `""` for path packages |
1634	| `lockChecksum` | 64-hex from the lock `checksum`, or `null` for git/path |
1635	| `fileManifestSha256` | H(`native.dependency-file-manifest.v1`, sorted `[{path, contentSha256, byteLength}]`) |
1636	| `fileCount`, `totalBytes` | exact uint64 |
1637	| `acquisition` | `{mode: in-snapshot-path \| in-snapshot-vendored \| imported-descriptor, descriptorId: ImportId\|null, vendorPath\|null}` |
1638	| `checksumVerification` | `tarball-matched \| self-consistent \| not-applicable \| mismatch` — `mismatch` refuses the whole set |
1639	| `provenanceAssurance` | `registry-authenticated \| declared` |
1640	
1641	Verification rules (feedback 3 corrected):
1642	
1643	- **DS-1 (registry, vendored tree)** A vendored directory carries a self-asserted
1644	  `.cargo-checksum.json`. Its `package` field equalling `lockChecksum` proves
1645	  nothing about the files: an attacker rewrites file contents and every `files`
1646	  entry while preserving `package`. The host therefore checks internal
1647	  consistency only (`package == lockChecksum`, every listed file's SHA-256
1648	  matches, no extra or missing files) and records `checksumVerification =
1649	  self-consistent`, `provenanceAssurance = declared`. Inconsistency is `mismatch`
1650	  and refuses the set. The reference model contains the mutation
1651	  (`ds1-mutation-preserving-package-checksum-stays-declared`): the mutated tree is
1652	  still admitted, and it is still *declared*, never authenticated.
1653	- **DS-2 (registry, tarball)** Only the exact `.crate` tarball whose SHA-256
1654	  equals `lockChecksum` yields `tarball-matched` / `registry-authenticated`. The
1655	  host extracts it deterministically into the CAS and computes the file manifest
1656	  itself. An extracted tree plus `.cargo-checksum.json` is DS-1.
1657	- **DS-3 (git)** The import supplies the checked-out tree for the exact `#rev`;
1658	  `not-applicable` / `declared`; the file manifest identity is the binding.
1659	- **DS-4 (path)** Path dependencies live in the snapshot; nothing is imported.
1660	- **DS-5 (no ambient reads)** `$CARGO_HOME/registry`, `~/.cargo`, `vendor/`
1661	  outside the snapshot, or any host path is read **only** as the explicit,
1662	  user-named source path of an import step (§7). Any acquisition mode outside the
1663	  closed set, or any fetch URL, refuses. No network fetch exists in any first-party
1664	  code path (design invariant, conformance-checked; not a confinement claim).
1665	- **DS-6 (completeness)** The set is complete for a target when every package
1666	  activated by `UnifiedFeaturesV1` is present with `checksumVerification ≠
1667	  mismatch`. An incomplete set is admitted with `completeness.incomplete` and
1668	  typed `input-closure-incomplete` Coverage for dependent crates; it never blocks
1669	  syntax analysis.
1670	
1671	`declared` provenance is disclosed wherever the package matters: in the Plan
1672	(through the set descriptor), in `AuthorizedExecutionV2.owners[].provenanceAssurance`,
1673	and in the pre-execution sentence (§5.2). Facts derived from declared sources are
1674	still Plan-bound Coverage inputs; the disclosure is what changes.

1676	### 3.2 Custody and transport
1677	
1678	The host stores admitted dependency sources in its content-addressed store keyed
1679	by `fileManifestSha256`; Plan-bound by `dependencySourceSetId`. Transport uses
1680	protocol-3 frames `DependencySourceManifest / DependencySourceChunk /
1681	DependencySourceSeal / DependencySourceAccepted` (§9.2) with the same byte-exact,
1682	digest-verified, reject-before-use discipline as the snapshot. The worker mounts
1683	the accepted files read-only at `.opensip/deps/v1/<name>-<version>/…` in its
1684	private scratch materialization. Nothing is fetched lazily.

1686	### 3.3 Cargo configuration: verified carrier, exact flags (feedback 5, 10)
1687	
1688	Primary source (`doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html`, read 2026-09-06):
1689	Cargo reads `.cargo/config.toml` (and legacy `.cargo/config`) from the current
1690	directory and **every ancestor**, plus `$CARGO_HOME/config.toml`, merging arrays;
1691	it also honors `CARGO_*` environment overrides and knobs that select executables
1692	(`build.rustc`, `build.rustc-wrapper`, `target.*.linker`, `target.*.runner`),
1693	credentials and network. Stock Cargo has no switch that disables ancestor
1694	discovery, and this contract does not claim `--config` replaces the stack.
1695	
1696	The first-party `opensip-cargo-adapter` therefore establishes a **verified
1697	ancestor carrier** (`CargoConfigProjectionV2`, all checked by
1698	`cargo_config_admission` in the model):
1699	
1700	- **CC-1** Before every Cargo invocation, every ancestor directory of the private
1701	  scratch root is checked for `.cargo/config.toml` and `.cargo/config`. Presence
1702	  is a refusal (`native.ambient-cargo-config`, exit 4), never a merge and never a
1703	  silent skip. `ancestorCarrierVerified=true` is recorded in the context.
1704	- **CC-2** `CARGO_HOME` is a fresh private empty directory created for the
1705	  invocation; its `config.toml` is absent by construction.
1706	- **CC-3** The constructed environment contains no `PATH`, `CARGO_*`, `RUSTFLAGS`,
1707	  `RUSTC*`, `RUSTDOC*`, `RUSTUP_*`, `CC`/`CXX`/`LD`/`AR`/`TARGET_*` variables;
1708	  presence of any is a refusal. Tool locations are passed as absolute closure
1709	  paths on the command line, not via environment.
1710	- **CC-4** Every selected tool digest equals its entry in `ToolClosureV1`.
1711	- **CC-5** Every `.cargo/config(.toml)` inside the snapshot (any directory, not
1712	  only the root) is replaced in the materialization by the single projected file;
1713	  the originals remain snapshot bytes for identity but are never read by Cargo.

1715	Projected (honored) keys: `build.target`, `build.rustflags`,
1716	`target.<triple>.rustflags` (both through the flag allowlist below),
1717	`source.<name>.directory` pointing inside the snapshot with `replace-with`,
1718	`resolver`, and `[patch]` in `Cargo.toml`. Stripped and recorded: `alias`,
1719	`build.rustc`, `build.rustc-wrapper`, `build.rustc-workspace-wrapper`,
1720	`build.rustdoc`, `build.target-dir`, `build.build-dir`, `build.incremental`,
1721	`build.dep-info-basedir`, `cargo-new`, `credential-alias`, `doc`, `env`,

1775	### 3.6 `PreparedOutputSetV3`: inert rows only (feedback 4, R2)
1776	
1777	Domain `native.prepared-output-set.v3` (revised in place; v3 was never accepted).
1778	`{schemaVersion:3, preparation: {kind: authorized-execution|imported-descriptor,
1779	authorizationId|null, importId|null, toolchain, dependencySourceSetId, cfgSetId,
1780	producer}, rows: [PreparedOutputRowV3…]}`.
1781	
1782	`PreparedOutputRowV3`: `{kind, ownerKey, configuration, site|null, generated|null,
1783	inputBinding: {ownerFileManifestSha256, dependencySourceSetId, toolchainDigest,
1784	cfgSetId}, blob: {sha256, byteLength, mediaType}, status: ok|failed,
1785	failureDetail|null}`.

1787	- **PO-0 (inert by kind and consumption channel; a media type is a label, never a
1788	  trust proof)** Admissible row kinds are exactly three:
1789	  `build-script-directives` (`text/x-cargo-directives`: the captured `cargo:`
1790	  lines, including `rustc-cfg`/`rustc-env` consumed by `cfg`/`env!`),
1791	  `macro-expansion` (`text/x-rust-expansion`: the fully expanded token text for one
1792	  invocation `site` = `{path, startByte, endByte, inputTokenDigest}`), and
1793	  `generated-file` (`generated = {logicalPath, blob}` with media type
1794	  `text/x-rust-source`, `text/plain` or `application/octet-stream`: one data file
1795	  a build script wrote under `OUT_DIR`). Row kinds `proc-macro-dylib` and
1796	  `build-script-binary` are refused **regardless of the media type they claim**
1797	  (a dylib relabelled `text/x-rust-expansion` is still a dylib row), and a media
1798	  type outside the kind's set is refused; either is
1799	  `native.prepared-output-not-inert` (exit 2), from an import *and* from the
1800	  in-host step alike (`generated-file-media-type-is-not-trust-proof-kind-decides`).
1801	  **No prepared artifact is ever loaded, linked or executed by the semantic
1802	  worker.** Expansions are looked up by exact
1803	  `(path, span, inputTokenDigest, macro crate manifest)`; a miss is a
1804	  `macro-expansion-unavailable` edge (L-RS4).
1805	- **PO-4 (generated-file input closure and the read-only virtual `OUT_DIR`)**
1806	  The worker resolves `env!("OUT_DIR")` for owner *O* to the read-only virtual
1807	  path `.opensip/out/v1/<ownerKey>/` in its sealed VFS. A site
1808	  `include!(concat!(env!("OUT_DIR"), "/generated.rs"))` (likewise
1809	  `include_str!`/`include_bytes!`) reads the `generated-file` row bound to
1810	  `(ownerKey, logicalPath="generated.rs")` whose `inputBinding` equals the current
1811	  context, and consumes its bytes **only** as Rust source text, a string literal or
1812	  a byte literal respectively. A miss (no row, stale binding, failed owner) is a
1813	  typed unknown: `build-script-generated-unavailable` edge, cause
1814	  `generated-file-missing`; it is never a hard failure and never a fallback to a
1815	  host path (`generated-file-include-out-dir-resolves-inert`,
1816	  `generated-file-missing-is-typed-unknown-not-failure`). Strict bounds
1817	  (`GeneratedInputBoundsV1`): `logicalPath` is a strict relative path (no `/`
1818	  prefix, no `.`/`..` segment, no NUL or backslash, ≤ 1024 bytes; an escaping path
1819	  fails exact typed admission and the worker lookup independently refuses it with
1820	  cause `generated-file-out-of-bounds`), `maxGeneratedFilesPerOwner 4096`,
1821	  `maxGeneratedFileBytes 67108864`, `maxGeneratedTotalBytes 1073741824`,
1822	  `maxGeneratedFileRows 1000000` (protocol limit). Imported blobs are bound to
1823	  archive members by exact `blobs[]` digest; an archive member outside the
1824	  wrapper's `blobs` is never read (`generated-file-path-escape-and-bounds-refused`).
1825	- **PO-1 (staleness)** A row is usable only if `inputBinding` equals the current
1826	  context (owner manifest, dependency set, toolchain digest, cfg set). A stale row
1827	  is refused before Plan construction (`REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED`, detail
1828	  `native.stale-prepared-output`, listing the differing fields) when prepared mode
1829	  was selected explicitly, or is ignored with a disclosed `staleRows` list and
1830	  non-prepared fallback when prepared mode was defaulted. It never uses a stale blob.

1839	Where do the expansions and generated files come from? From the **preparation
1840	step** (§5.3), which is the only place proc-macro dylibs are built and loaded and

1842	boundaries. The step captures the required generated **data** and discards every

1848	## 4. Resolution completeness (AR-12)
1849	
1850	### 4.1 Two different completeness claims
1851	
1852	A Coverage entry commits two things that were previously conflated:
1853	
1854	1. **Examined universe** — the exhaustive examined subject/target partition
1855	   (`subjectScopeCommitment`, retained). "Did we look at every subject?"
1856	2. **Resolution completeness** — whether every reference/import/call edge
1857	   originating in the examined subjects was resolved to a binding at the requested
1858	   rung, *after resolution was actually attempted over the whole partition*.
1859	   "Could we see every consumer?"
1860	
1861	### 4.1a Producing recipe for `subjectScopeCommitment` (closed)
1862	
1863	The retained C-2 selector deferred computation and verification. This is the successor
1864	recipe; nothing about the historical artifact changes.
1865	
1866	**Recipe.** `subjectScopeCommitment` is the foundation **subject-scope** identity of the
1867	examined partition, re-spelled in the native `Sha256Text` text form:
1868	
1869	```
1870	scope2      = identity-and-evidence H("subject-scope", D)          -> "scope2:"  + hex
1871	commitment  = "sha256:" + the same 64 hex                          -> Sha256Text
1872	```
1873	
1874	where `D` is the closed foundation record
1875	`identity-schemas.v3.json#/$defs/subject-scope`
1876	`{schemaVersion: 2, snapshotId, sourceUniverse, targetUniverse, relation, resolution,
1877	enumeratorClosure, subjects}`.
1878	
1879	**Inputs, exactly, and where each comes from.** `snapshotId` is the admitted `snapshot2`.
1880	`relation`/`resolution` are the Coverage key's own relation and rung. `sourceUniverse` and
1881	`targetUniverse` are the bare 64-hex universe digests of the same key (§2, §11).
1882	`enumeratorClosure` is the `closure2` of the Plan-bound enumerator that produced the
1883	partition. `subjects` is the **complete** examined subject inventory that enumerator
1884	enumerated over that snapshot, a canonical set (foundation ordering, duplicates refuse
1885	rather than dedupe). **Encoding**: the foundation canonical encoder and `H` frame, imported,
1886	not restated. There is **no native `H` domain for this field**: one preimage, one digest,
1887	two admitted textual spellings (§11).
1888	
1889	**Join with `scope2`.** The commitment is the *identical* digest to the `scope2` the host
1890	binds into the `coverage2` descriptor (`coverage.scopeId`). It is therefore not a second
1891	commitment and cannot drift from the scope it names. Its purpose is that the Coverage
1892	*payload* — the bytes whose `payloadDigest` mints `coverage2` — carries the provider's
1893	in-band commitment to the partition it claims to have examined, which the host then checks
1894	against a value the provider never supplied.
1895	
1896	**Where it is produced and checked (`admit_coverage_result_v3`, the admitted native producer
1897	boundary).** For every `CoverageResultV3` a provider sends, before any `coverage2` exists:
1898	
1899	1. The host builds `D` from **its own** enumeration and mints `scope2`. A provider-supplied
1900	   commitment is never an input to this step.
1901	2. `key.relation`, `key.resolution`, `key.sourceUniverse`, `key.targetUniverse` must equal
1902	   `D`'s (`native.coverage-key-scope-mismatch:<field>`).
1903	3. `key.subjectScopeCommitment` must equal the computed commitment
1904	   (`native.subject-scope-commitment-mismatch`).
1905	4. `entry.examinedUniverse.subjectScopeCommitment` must equal the key's
1906	   (`native.examined-universe-commitment-mismatch`) and
1907	   `entry.examinedUniverse.subjectCount` must equal `len(D.subjects)`
1908	   (`native.examined-universe-subject-count-mismatch`). A provider that examined a narrower
1909	   partition than the host enumerated is detected here, and by nothing else.
1910	5. RC-2 (§4.3) is rechecked over the same partition.
1911	6. Only then is `coverage2` minted from `{schemaVersion: 2, scopeId, payloadSchemaDigest,
1912	   payloadDigest}`. `payloadSchemaDigest` is the raw SHA-256 of the **exact registered schema
1913	   DOCUMENT bytes** (§7.2). A caller may restate it but never choose it: a value that is not the
1914	   registered document's digest refuses `native.coverage-payload-schema-not-registered`
1915	   (`coverage-payload-schema-digest-a-caller-chose-is-refused`).
1916	
1917	Every refusal above is `PROVIDER.PROTOCOL_VIOLATION` (`operational-failed` 4) under the §10
1918	fault law: a worker that lies about its partition contributes no facts, no Coverage and no
1919	Run. This is not a Coverage deficiency; an admitted-but-incomplete input is (§10).
1920	
1921	**Coverage use (`coverage_view_use`).** A `view2` may name a `coverage2` only if that
1922	`coverage2` was admitted at the boundary above and its `scope2` is one of the view's own
1923	`scopeIds`. A hash-valid `coverage2` whose subject scope sits outside the evaluated view is
1924	refused exactly as hidden finding evidence is (identity §3), rather than joined silently.
1925	
1926	**No circularity.** `D` names the snapshot, the universes and the enumerator closure. A
1927	universe descriptor (§2) names its native context, tools and config projection; a native
1928	context names closures; none of them names a scope, a Coverage, a view, an evidence record
1929	or a Run. The derivation order is therefore total and acyclic: closures → native context →
1930	universe → `scope2` → commitment → Coverage payload → `coverage2` → `view2`. The foundation
1931	scope *descriptor* whose raw digest is `scopeDigest` (§1.4, workspace roots and path
1932	prefixes) is a different record with a different job and is not this commitment.

1957	refusal vocabulary and the coverage-use join) and adds no second recipe. Any future divergence
1958	between them is a defect in whichever document moved.

1961	B does `import * as m from './a'` then `m[k]()` with `k` a runtime string. Every
1962	subject is examined, `m` resolves, `m[k]` has no admissible fact at any rung of

1964	predicate is *satisfied*. Under this contract the provider must emit an

1969	versus v2).

2455	The mandatory pre-execution sentence, in human and

2764	`HelloV3` also carries `identityVersions: {snapshot:2, plan:2, fact:2, coverage:3}`
2765	and `HelloAckV3` must echo the token array and identity versions exactly.

2767	`plan-identity-plan2`, `fact-identity-fact2`, and `coverage-v3`.

2769	an identity token, is not required to spawn, and does not enlarge the

2772	occupancy is unknown except exact-id ephemeral. A FactBatchV3 payload

2795	   `NativeContextVerified`, then Analyze.

3328	**A refused value can exceed the diagnostic bound, and the projection is
3329	bounded.** `DomainDetail.subject` is `BoundedText` (1024) while a *structurally
3330	valid* `languageMode` may be 4096 characters; the composed subject then reached
3331	4149 and made the whole failure envelope schema-invalid at
3332	`termination.domainDetail.subject` or `errors[0].subject`. `bounded_subject`
3333	elides: the registered **key** is preserved verbatim — it selects the code, the
3334	class and the origin — and only the offending value is elided, keeping a leading
3335	window plus the SHA-256 of the untruncated subject's UTF-8 bytes. Emitting the untruncated
3336	string would be schema-invalid, dropping the subject would lose attribution, and
3337	reclassifying the input error as success would be false. The code, class and
3338	origin are never changed by the elision.
3339	
3340	The encoding is normative, and its **units** are stated because they differ
3341	between the two operations. Let `raw` be the composed subject
3342	`<registered key>[:<value>]` as an **admitted Unicode scalar string**. Length and
3343	slicing count **Unicode code points**, which is what `BoundedText`'s JSON Schema
3344	`maxLength` counts — not UTF-8 bytes and not UTF-16 code units. If
3345	`len(raw) ≤ 1024` the subject **is** `raw`. Otherwise it is
3346	
3347	```
3348	raw[: 1024 − len("...#sha256:") − 64] + "...#sha256:" + hex(SHA256(raw.encode("utf-8")))
3349	```
3350	
3351	— the marker `...#sha256:` is ASCII, the digest is exactly 64 lowercase hex
3352	characters, the SHA-256 input is exactly `raw` encoded as UTF-8 with **no**
3353	additional normalization, and the result is exactly 1024 code points. A
3354	non-ASCII value therefore has a UTF-8 byte length that may exceed 1024 while its
3355	scalar length does not, and the two operations must not be conflated.
3356	
3357	Two distinct long values are distinguished under the **ordinary
3358	collision-resistance assumption** for SHA-256; this is not a claim that collision
3359	is impossible. **The guarantee is confined to what is published** — the bounded
3360	subject and its digest. This contract does **not** promise a separate retained
3361	store of the untruncated value and names none; a host that keeps its own
3362	operational log may match it by recomputing this digest, which is why the digest
3363	is published at all.

3481	(`scopeCapabilityLaw`; `COVERAGE_SOURCE_VARIANT_UNSUPPORTED_SCOPE`,
3482	`…_DEFICIENCY_MISMATCH`, `…_CAUSE_MISMATCH`, and
3483	`native.coverage-source-variant-*` at the producer boundary).** The per-body
3484	selector already refused an unlisted suffix — `BODY_LANGUAGE_SOURCE_VARIANT_UNKNOWN`
3485	for TypeScript, `BODY_LANGUAGE_GRAMMAR_VARIANT_UNKNOWN` for the syntax universe —
3486	but that selector is reached only while a body is being derived, and a scope that
3487	produces **no fact** derives none. A `clones` scope over `package.json` under the
3488	TypeScript universe was therefore classified by nothing at all and could seal a
3489	determinate `complete` over an empty view: a finding of *no clones* in a file that
3490	universe cannot read as TypeScript in any dialect. Coverage is a claim about the
3491	**examination**, so it must not be decided by whether the examination happened to
3492	produce output. The disclosed pair is the existing
3493	`language-tier-unsupported` / `capability-missing` — no new deficiency, no new
3494	`nativeCause`, no new public detail code — and it is *read from* the published law
3495	rather than restated by the model.
3496	
3497	This is deliberately **not** the treatment `BODY_LANGUAGE_OWNER_NOT_COMPILED`
3498	gets two paragraphs above, and the difference is substantive rather than
3499	stylistic. That refusal is about a path which **is** a Rust source file and which
3500	no *selected* target compiles: the universe examined a known-language file and
3501	correctly produced no fact, so `complete` stays lawful. A suffix outside the
3502	table is not a body of that universe in any dialect, so a determinate answer
3503	would assert a negative the universe never had the capability to establish —
3504	exactly the principle the syntax capability law already encodes. The gate is the
3505	relation registry's `bodyIdentityJoin`, so the law reaches only where the dialect
3506	axis is consulted at all (today, `clones`); it claims nothing about symbol
3507	capability, executes and qualifies no compiler or parser, and leaves inventory
3508	evidence ungated on every inventoried path. A `source-path` scope is judged on
3509	**all** of its own subjects, so a mixed `src/a.ts` + `package.json` scope
3510	discloses rather than hiding its unsupported half, an empty subject list is
3511	unsupported rather than vacuously complete, and a **supported** path with no
3512	clone body in it remains a lawful `complete`.
3513	
3514	**Fault law (R7; `stage_authority`, `run_termination`, `StageAuthorityV1`).**
3515	A worker that faults — process fault, protocol violation, `ProviderFault` frame,
3516	crash — contributes **no facts, no Coverage entries and no Run**: its diagnostics
3517	(stderr, fault detail) are an operational record only and can never mint an
3518	authoritative fact; the invocation is `operational-failed` (4)
3519	`PROVIDER.PROTOCOL_VIOLATION`; cancellation is `interrupted` (130) with the same
3520	no-facts rule (`fault-worker-diagnostics-never-mint-facts-or-run`). By contrast a
3521	stage that terminates cleanly over **successfully admitted but incomplete inputs**
3522	(missing crate, generated file unavailable, unresolved edges) yields admitted
3523	facts and typed Coverage, seals an **authoritative** Run, and terminates
3524	`indeterminate` (3) with the deficiency as typed detail in the coverage2 record
3525	(`admitted-incomplete-inputs-yield-authoritative-indeterminate-3`).
3526	`BudgetExhausted` and `Unavailable` are clean typed terminals: facts before the
3527	terminal are admitted and the Run is authoritative with the stage `partial`.
3528	The stage's native termination code is the route above applied to its native primary
3529	deficiency: `VERDICT.INDETERMINATE` for the incomplete-input deficiencies named here, and
3530	`COVERAGE.BUDGET_EXHAUSTED` / `COVERAGE.PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE` for those two terminals unless an entry
3531	declares a more specific deficiency (`run-termination-code-is-the-primary-deficiency-route`). The Run's
3532	termination is the host's D9 reduction over all its conditions (section 10, native stage selection).

3641	`edition` is a map from crate **name** to year, so it is the *selected value*
3642	that is the dialect, never the map: a body identity that varied with unrelated
3643	crates would be neither meaningful nor representable. When the map's distinct
3644	value set has exactly one member — the ordinary case, including a large
3645	single-edition workspace — that member is the dialect of every body and no owner
3646	selection arises. When it has more than one, the **owning compilation unit
3647	decides**.
3648	
3649	More precisely, the **compilation target** decides, not the package. Cargo
3650	documents an `edition` on a target that **defaults to** `package.edition` when
3651	absent — `cargo metadata` lists `targets[].edition` and states the package value
3652	is a default individual targets may differ from, and the `[[bin]]`/`[lib]`
3653	`edition` field, though deprecated, is still documented. So *source → package →
3654	package edition* misses a supported override, and a universe whose package
3655	defaults **all agree** can still contain a target that does not. There is
3656	therefore **no single-edition fast path**: a `clones` fact over a Rust universe
3657	requires the committed ownership relation whatever the package map looks like,
3658	and a null `sourceUnitOwnershipId` admits no clone.
3659	
3660	`SourceUnitOwnershipV1` is that relation **and the explicit selection**, and
3661	`RustUniverseV2ResolvedInputs.sourceUnitOwnershipId` is the `h-identity` of
3662	`native.source-unit-ownership.v1` that carries it — required and nullable,
3663	exactly as `preparedOutputSetId` is. It holds three things:
3664	
3665	- `units` — the **closed table of compilation targets**:
3666	  `{unitId, markerPath, crateName, targetKind, targetName, targetEdition}`.
3667	  `targetEdition` is the target's own edition when it sets one and `null` when it
3668	  takes the package default, so the two committed places can never contradict.
3669	- `selectedUnitIds` — the **explicit analysis scope**, non-empty, every member a
3670	  declared `unitId`.
3671	- `ownership` — the pure relation `{path, unitId}`, carrying no edition and no
3672	  metadata, so it cannot contradict the table.
3673	
3674	`unitId` is **derived, never declared**:
3675	
3676	```
3677	unitId = H(native.compilation-unit.v1,
3678	           UnitIdentityV1{schemaVersion: 1, markerPath, targetKind, targetName})
3679	```
3680	
3681	carried as `sha256:<64 hex>`, with **`derived` retention**: nothing separate is
3682	retained, because the preimage *is* the unit row, and admission re-derives and
3683	compares (`sourceUnitOwnership.unitId`). **This is not an opaque digest** — the
3684	preimage record, its domain, its codec and its selector are all published here,
3685	so any consumer rebuilds it from the row that carries it.
3686	
3687	An earlier draft joined the fields with delimiters,
3688	`markerPath#targetKind:targetName`. **That is withdrawn.** It was injective only
3689	by excluding `#` from `markerPath`, and a `#` in a repository directory is
3690	admissible under the canonical repository-path contract — so the recipe narrowed
3691	admitted paths in order to make a delimiter work, which is the wrong trade. `H`
3692	needs no such restriction, is fixed width for every admitted path and name
3693	length, and a marker under a `#`-containing directory closes a complete Run.
3694	
3695	`units` is strictly unique by `unitId`, and `unitId` is a function of the
3696	metadata, so **two contradictory rows for one purported unit are a refusal, never
3697	two units that differ by accident**, and a selection or ownership row naming an
3698	undeclared `unitId` is an unbound caller label and inadmissible.
3699	
3700	`markerPath` is the inventoried manifest that declares the target — the same
3701	vocabulary `WorkspaceUnitV2` already uses, under the ordinary canonical
3702	repository-path admission with no added restriction. **`WorkspaceUnitV2` and
3703	`UnitMembershipV1` cannot supply this binding**, and that is a granularity
3704	statement rather than an oversight: they identify *workspace* units
3705	(`cargo-package`, `cargo-workspace`), while one package holds several targets
3706	that may carry different editions. Naming the marker joins my targets to that
3707	existing discovery vocabulary instead of competing with it.
3708	
3709	**Because the selection is committed inside the record whose `h-identity` the
3710	universe names, a different selection is a different record, a different identity
3711	and therefore a different `sourceUniverse`.** That is what makes the required case
3712	representable: one physical source path compiled by two targets at two editions is
3713	validly analysed **under each selection, one at a time**, each with its own
3714	correct dialect and its own body identity, and **no relation payload changed** to
3715	make it so.
3716	
3717	Selection is exact and total, and the order of decision is fixed so each step has
3718	its own cause. No committed ownership refuses. `enumeration: partial` refuses
3719	**before any row is read**. Rows are those whose `path` **equals** the enclosing
3720	fact's anchor path — never a prefix, never a nearest directory, never a first
3721	match — and no row at all refuses as not-compiled. Rows are then restricted to
3722	`selectedUnitIds`, and a path compiled only by **unselected** targets refuses as
3723	not-selected rather than borrowing an out-of-scope edition. Selected owners whose
3724	effective editions **agree** are admissible — the ordinary shared-file and
3725	lib-plus-test-target case. Selected owners that **disagree** are an ambiguous
3726	unselected request and refuse. §2.1's retained-input admission independently
3727	requires every marker and owned path to be a source of the same snapshot, every
3728	selection and ownership row to name a declared unit, and every deferring unit to
3729	name a crate the same `edition` map declares.
3730	
3731	**Selected scope is not incomplete enumeration.** A selection says these targets
3732	*are* the analysis, so an owner outside them is deliberately out of scope; it is
3733	committed in the identity, so every consumer sees it and it changes the universe.
3734	`partial` says the producer did not finish, so an owner *inside* the selected
3735	scope may exist that is not listed and could contradict a listed one — a gap in
3736	knowledge, invisible as a selection, admitting no dialect at all. Silently
3737	omitting a conflicting owner from the table is not a selection either: an
3738	omission leaves no trace, whereas a selection is part of the universe identity.
3739	Partial evidence stays useful under the existing law rather than voiding a Run —
3740	the clones scope mints no body identity, its Coverage carries the incompleteness,
3741	and the predicate and seal are indeterminate.
3742	
3743	The consequence is the one that matters: an **ordinary mixed-edition workspace
3744	has a representable valid form**. Each path is owned by units of one edition, so
3745	bodies of *both* editions are admissible in the *same* universe, each carrying
3746	its own dialect. Only a path genuinely compiled under two different editions
3747	refuses, which is a real ambiguity in the input rather than a gap in the law.
3748	This record states what a producer claims it enumerated; it admits no compiler,
3749	measures no build and qualifies no enumerator.
3750	
3751	Exact typed admission precedes every schema check and is imported, not
3752	reimplemented: `canonical.parse` refuses `1.0`, `1e0`, `-0`, non-finite tokens,
3753	duplicate keys and lone surrogates; `canonical.validate` uses the exact-const /
3754	exact-enum / exact-integer validator so `true` is never an integer and `1.0` is
3755	never `1` (`float-spelled-integer-refused`). Every native record schema is closed
3756	(`additionalProperties:false`, checked by the report's `openObjects=[]`).

3916	dependency manifests are pruned first and never count, §1.4 U-4a/U-7), while an

3928	incomplete analysis, never an undisclosed truncation. Reviewed candidate identities
3929	follow a stable source fingerprint within a project, separately from the current
3930	Run, under the workflow review contract.

3932	Cross-unit reference evidence: `docs/coop/design-corrections/integration-host-model.py`
3933	and `check-integration.py`. The model composes actual reference admissions over
3934	synthetic TCB inputs; it does not execute repository code or measure confinement.
3935	
3936	Public details for the shared cap and explicit-root grammar are PROJECT.WORKSPACE_UNIT_LIMIT and PROJECT.EXPLICIT_PATH_INVALID. The pure instrument retains native.too-many-units and native.explicit-root-grammar only as internal aliases; the host normalizes them through public-detail-registry.v1.json, and the public schema rejects those aliases. The internal capability table key provider-unavailable/capability-missing emits native.capability-unavailable publicly.
3937	
3938	The four repository-code child-process effect selections in §5 are consistent with the accepted permission-truth-tables.v9 head. The v7→v9 changes concern metadata/recording and the host-under-instruction network recital; the permission table rows supplying the four selections are unchanged. The product still declares these as its own supported-platform design selections, not measured confinement or an extension of preview qualification.
3939	
3940	
3941	A **bounded selection array** that exceeds its published schema bound refuses REQUEST.UNSATISFIABLE (request-rejected, exit2), public detail PROJECT.SCOPE_LIMIT and subject `field:count>limit`; it is never truncated. **Seven** fields are bounded this way, across **three record families**, and the subject always names which one overflowed. The public code is shared across host/native scope admission; callers must narrow explicit selection — for `requestedCapabilities` that means fewer workspace roots for the invocation, or an explicit `analysis.capabilities` selection carrying its own provenance. The **Plan** family contributes the remaining three, and they are reachable by ordinary valid selections that every earlier bound admits: `nativeContextDigests` has limit128 and carries one member per DISTINCT admitted native context, so an inventory-only or otherwise narrow capability selection keeps `requestedCapabilities` far below its own1024 while129 units whose compiler closure, standard library and effective options differ pass the workspace bound and cannot be expressed in the Plan; `importIds` has limit256 while the selecting field `semantic-configuration.evidence.importIds` admits1024, so257 imported evidence records are an admitted configuration and an unrepresentable Plan; and `semanticClosures` has limit128 while `policyPackIds` admits128 packs that need not share closures. Those three are accounted **before plan2 is minted**, on the PROSPECTIVE Plan assembled from an already-admitted request, so a refusal mints no Plan and no Run for the refused step. They are **not** a retained-record check: an externally retained Plan over its bound is a corrupt or malformed retained record and keeps its schema-first refusal and this section's origin-dependent routing, because re-deriving a caller's remedy from already-committed bytes would misreport a corrupt store as an oversized request. Only an ACTUAL array over its bound refuses on cardinality; a missing field, null, boolean, number, string or object is a shape the schema owns and reaches it untouched. When more than one array of an assembled prospective Plan overflows at once the subject is the first in the published `$defs/plan` declaration order — `semanticClosures`, `nativeContextDigests`, `importIds` — so one request always yields one subject and narrowing makes deterministic progress. That order governs the prospective-Plan boundary, among the fields present there. It is not an ordering claim about the whole request: `nativeContextDigests` is also accounted at the earlier producer boundary that computes, admission-validates and deduplicates the native contexts, and an overflow refuses there before any prospective Plan is assembled. Native ScopeRefusal retains detail, D9 and observed bound fields for the host's closed termination projection, and is already field-generic, so all seven fields use one law and one code: the remedy class is identical — narrow the selection explicitly, nothing was truncated — which is why widening it across the further record families adds no public code, while each field keeps its OWN remedy wording because what a caller narrows differs per field.
3942	
3943	The **pre-Plan admission order** is published, because it is what makes the typed refusal reachable. A complete `analysis-spec` - defaulted or explicitly supplied - is admitted in three steps: **bounded selection cardinality first**, then generic schema validation of the whole record, then the closed native capability vocabulary. Cardinality precedes schema validation because a `maxItems` breach is reported generically: the exception restates the entire instance and carries no typed scope projection — no public detail, class, exit, `field:count>limit` subject or per-field remedy — even though its own structured fields do identify the failing path and the bound; an oversized ordinary selection is not a malformed record and is not published as one. The first step is **conditional on the field actually being a JSON array in an object**, and nothing is coerced: a missing field, a null, a boolean, a number, a string or an object proceeds untouched to the schema step and refuses there as the malformed record it is. Without that condition a 1025-character string would be published as 1025 capabilities, which is a misclassification and not a scope limit. Everything a schema is genuinely better at - an unknown property, a wrong type, a missing field, a missing `schemaVersion` - still refuses at the schema step exactly as before, **for every input that reaches that step**. Which inputs those are follows from the condition, not from the bound alone: step 1 refuses **only** an actual JSON array that is over its bound, so a spec whose `requestedCapabilities` is **absent, null, a boolean, a number, a string or an object** proceeds untouched to the schema step and refuses there as the malformed record it is, and so does an array **within** its bound that is malformed in any other way. The ordering is exact and cardinality-first, so an input that is *both* an oversized array and otherwise malformed refuses with the cardinality result - `PROJECT.SCOPE_LIMIT`, subject `field:count>limit` - and its schema fault is reported on a later, narrowed request rather than in the same one. Nothing is lost or misclassified by that: the malformed spec is refused either way, no Plan or Run is minted for the refused step, and the refusal that does fire states a true fact about the instance. **The two routes are not, however, the same public termination, and this paragraph does not flatten them.** The cardinality refusal is origin-independent - `request-rejected` (2), `REQUEST.UNSATISFIABLE`, `PROJECT.SCOPE_LIMIT` - because an oversized ordinary selection is not malformed. The schema refusal keeps §10's **origin-dependent** routing: an externally supplied or retained spec is `request-rejected` (2) / `REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED`, while a host-generated internal layer minting its own invalid spec is **`operational-failed` (4)** / `SYSTEM.OUTCOME.ILLEGAL_STATE` with `faultCause: host-invariant`. Reordering the two steps therefore never converts a host-invariant fault into a request rejection, and never the reverse. One condition is reordered for one shape, and none is added. This order is the **request** boundary only. Validation of a **retained** `analysis-spec` payload at Run closure is a different question with a different answer - an oversized array there means corruption rather than an oversized request - and nothing here changes it: Run closure schema-validates the retained record before any capability vocabulary admission, so an over-long retained array already refuses there.
3944	
3945	What this refusal is **not**. It is not a truncation: no capability is dropped, no root is dropped, and the matrix-fixed default and every advertised capability promise are unchanged. It is not a host defect: the host computed the default correctly and the *request* simply cannot be expressed within a published bound, so it is `request-rejected`/`REQUEST.UNSATISFIABLE` and never `host-invariant`. It is not a licence to shard the invocation, execute extra steps or raise a bound — any of those would be a new product capability and none is selected here. And it is **pre-Plan for the analysis step it refuses**: that step mints no `plan2` and no `run3`. That is a statement about the step, not about attribution - the request and the invocation keep their ordinary operational attribution under the workflow law, and any earlier step of the same invocation that already committed an outcome keeps it. A pure helper `ValidationError` is not a public termination, which is exactly why the typed refusal exists.
3946	
3947	The standalone boundary-crossing key native.explicit-root-crosses-boundary is an internal alias of PROJECT.EXPLICIT_PATH_INVALID, the code security emits before native on the operational path. native.boundary-inventory-mismatch is an internal alias of PROJECT.DISCOVERY_INVENTORY_MISMATCH. The latter public condition is emitted by the actual host when its native marker/file inventory disagrees with the security discovery inventory (REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED, exit2), including before native is invoked. Neither internal spelling is a public enum value.

333	## S4. Trust time (AR-04)
334	
335	Definitions. `evalHighWater` (floor F): highest instant at which a decision
336	evaluation was made. `lastAccepted` (L): issue time of the newest accepted
337	signed document; required whenever F exists. **Admitted time evidence** A =
338	max(L, accepted witness time, presented root issue time), where a witness is
339	the newest issue time of a presented payload whose signature already verified
340	and which is not older than L. The wall clock is untrusted.
341	
342	Decision evaluation, in order, for record R, observation (wall W, sleep-
343	inclusive monotonic M, bootId B), optional payload P:
344	
345	1. Payload future check (unchanged FC-FUTURE): an issue time > W + 24 h refuses
346	   `PAYLOAD-NOT-ADMISSIBLE`; nothing is written.
347	2. Fresh install (F absent): without admitted time evidence the evaluation
348	   refuses `TRUST.NO_ADMITTED_TIME_CONTEXT` (the core's embedded bootstrap
349	   payload or an ordinary payload is required); nothing is written. With it,
350	   W > A + 90 d refuses `CLOCK-EXCURSION-FORWARD` and initialises nothing.
351	   Otherwise tEval = max(W, A); F := tEval, L := A, anchor := (B, M, W); expiry
352	   states are evaluated from the presented documents, never set to false.
353	3. In-session continuity: if the anchor has the same bootId, expected =
354	   anchorWall + (M − anchorMono). A forward deviation over 24 h refuses
355	   `CLOCK-EXCURSION-FORWARD` (`in-session`) unless a witness proves the
356	   expectation itself was behind (witness ≥ expected). A backward deviation is
357	   the finding `CLOCK-REGRESSION-IN-SESSION`; a monotonic value below the
358	   anchor's is `CLOCK-CONTINUITY-MALFORMED` (finding, anchor not rewritten).
359	4. Plausibility: W > A + 90 d refuses `CLOCK-EXCURSION-FORWARD`
360	   (`beyond-horizon`) **before any evaluation and before any write**. Remedy:
361	   correct the clock, or present a payload issued within 90 d of W.
362	5. Evaluation: tEval = max(F, W, A). The floor written is exactly tEval
363	   (write-ahead, §5.6 durability), so the persisted floor and the evaluated
364	   instant never differ and no later evaluation runs earlier than an earlier
365	   one. `CLOCK-REGRESSION` (W < F) and `TRUST.FLOOR_AHEAD_OF_WALL`
366	   (F > W + 90 d) are findings with remedies. L advances to A when A > L. The
367	   anchor is rewritten when continuity is unavailable, within tolerance, or
368	   excused by a witness.
369	
370	Consequences. An accidental forward wall is accepted only up to 90 d beyond
371	signed evidence, so a wrong write is bounded and heals as signed time catches
372	up; a larger jump writes nothing. Expiry, staleness and future checks still
373	fail closed at tEval. Repeated reboots cannot lower F or freeze payload
374	freshness: F only rises, and freshness is evaluated at tEval ≥ F. Report-only
375	evaluation (doctor) computes the same decision, states and findings, labels
376	`evaluationMode: report-only`, and returns `writes: []` with every write field
377	null; it cannot create a recovery challenge.
378	
379	### S4.5 Recovery of an already poisoned floor
380	
381	A floor years ahead of real time (written by the superseded rule, or by a
382	restore) cannot be lowered by ordinary payloads: tEval ≥ F keeps every document
383	expired. Recovery is an authenticated, install-bound, single-use act:
384	
385	1. `opensip trust recovery-challenge` (decision mode only; global fence, no
386	   project lease) writes one pending challenge and exports
387	   `trust-recovery-challenge.v1.json` (`TrustRecoveryChallengeV1`): a fresh
388	   32-byte host-CSPRNG nonce, `createdWall`, and `recordDigest` =
389	   metadata-profile digest, domain `opensip.metadata.recovery-challenge.1`,
390	   over the six bound fields `{evalHighWater, lastAccepted, rootVersion,
391	   revocationVersion, indexSnapshotVersion, recoveryEpochSerial}`. The
392	   pending record additionally binds `{bootId, createdMono, expiresMono =
393	   createdMono + 24 h, createdWall}` with sleep-inclusive monotonic time. A
394	   new challenge replaces the pending one; a reboot invalidates it.
395	2. The publisher's recovery service (consented online) or the air-gap ceremony
396	   returns `trust-recovery-epoch.v1.json`: an `opensip-signature-envelope.2`
397	   of kind `trust-recovery-epoch` (digest domain
398	   `opensip.metadata.recovery-epoch.1`) with body `TrustRecoveryEpochV1`
399	   `{recoverySchema:1, kind, epochSerial, issuedAt, challenge{nonce,
400	   recordDigest}, counters{rootVersion, revocationVersion,
401	   indexSnapshotVersion}, installBinding:"challenge"}`. Authority is the
402	   **accepted root's `recoveryAuthority.keys` at `recoveryAuthority.threshold`**
403	   (the existing schema-1 field: 5–16 keys, threshold ≥ 3, disjoint from
404	   `rootKeys`), revoked keys excluded. Root keys never count, so routine
405	   recovery never exercises root keys and root-key compromise alone cannot
406	   lower a floor. The accepted root's expiry is not consulted for this one
407	   document because the floor under repair is what expired it. This is the
408	   only external artifact needed.
409	3. `opensip trust recovery-import` verifies, under the global fence and no
410	   project lease, in this order: (a) **strict closed shape of the epoch and of
411	   the pending record before any comparison** (exact-typed constants: `true`
412	   is never `1`, integers are never booleans, timestamps by grammar, hex by
413	   grammar); (b) recovery-authority threshold; (c) a pending challenge exists,
414	   its `bootId` equals the current boot, and `createdMono ≤ mono ≤
415	   expiresMono` (`CHALLENGE_BOOT_CHANGED`, `CHALLENGE_EXPIRED`,
416	   `CHALLENGE_CONTINUITY_MALFORMED`); (d) nonce equals the pending nonce;
417	   `recordDigest` equals both the pending value and a fresh digest of the
418	   current record; `epochSerial` > `recoveryEpochSerial`; (e) **every counter
419	   equals the challenged record's counter exactly** (`COUNTER_MISMATCH:<k>`).
420	   A higher signed counter is refused with that typed detail; the remedy is to

420	   A higher signed counter is refused with that typed detail; the remedy is to
421	   import the ordinary payload that carries it and re-challenge. Nothing is
422	   silently discarded and nothing is silently advanced. (f) `issuedAt` ≥ L and
423	   |`issuedAt` − W| ≤ 24 h (`ISSUED_IN_FUTURE`, `ISSUED_TOO_OLD_FOR_WALL`).
424	   Any failure refuses `RECOVERY.REFUSED` with the typed detail and changes
425	   nothing.
426	4. On success: F := L := `issuedAt`; anchor cleared; `recoveryEpochSerial` :=
427	   `epochSerial`; pending challenge consumed; audit record `RECOVERY-EPOCH`
428	   with the previous floor. Counters, revocation entries, role states,
429	   journals and namespaces are untouched; no namespace is deleted.
430	
431	Threat statement. The wall is untrusted. The single-boot, 24 h monotonic
432	challenge window plus the ±24 h issue skew mean that no response to an old
433	challenge, held indefinitely, can later lower the floor to a stale real time:
434	after a reboot or after the window the response is dead, and inside the window
435	the signed time must sit within a day of the wall the operator is looking at.
436	This bounds a signed epoch relative to the wall; it does not prove the wall.
437	The protocol promises install binding (nonce + record digest), single use,
438	serial monotonicity, exact counter preservation and no floor below L. It makes
439	**no promise against a malicious publisher**: a recovery authority that signs a
440	false time is outside the protocol, exactly as it is for every other signed
441	time in this contract. Why this cannot revive revoked trust: revocation is by
442	counter and entries, which the epoch may not change; a key revoked before the
443	epoch cannot sign it; expiry is re-evaluated at signed real time, which is ≥
444	every earlier signed time, so a document genuinely expired at real time stays
445	expired. If the recovery authority is unavailable, recovery is impossible and
446	the install must be re-established by fresh install or authenticated adoption.
447	Migration and rollback (S9) never carry a pending challenge; the serial moves
448	forward with the other floors.

450	## S5. Root chain through expired roots (AR-05)
451	
452	An install holding accepted root N evaluates a chain N+1..M link by link. Each
453	link needs the previous root's threshold from that root's keys (continuity)
454	**and** the new root's threshold from its own keys (possession), revoked keys
455	excluded from both. Semantic admission per link: reader supports the schema;
456	version and previous-version contiguity; not issued before its predecessor;
457	issue before expiry; root key policy. Intermediate expiry is never consulted;
458	the final root must be unexpired at tEval and not issued more than 24 h after
459	the wall. Any refusal leaves state unchanged and names the link. Success
460	advances the root counter to M and L to the final root's issue time. An expired
461	root with no chain refuses `ROOT.EXPIRED_NO_CHAIN` with the remedy of presenting
462	a payload carrying N+1..newest. Schema-1 readers refuse a schema-2 root as
463	`ROOT.SCHEMA_UNSUPPORTED` (typed, not corruption, state unchanged).
464	
465	## S6. Live revocation (AR-05)
466	
467	Trust epoch `{rootVersion, indexSnapshotVersion, revocationVersion,
468	permissionPolicyDigest}` is captured at operation start. **Authority
469	checkpoint:** every brokered effect request re-reads the epoch under the
470	journal append lock before its intent record. **Observer:** a tick every 5 s
471	reads the counter; if the last successful read is older than 10 s or the read
472	fails, the observer appends `REV(observer-fail-stop)` and cancels. These bounds
473	are implementation qualification obligations under OS scheduling assumptions
474	using `CLOCK_BOOTTIME` (Linux) / `mach_continuous_time` (macOS); they are not a
475	wall-clock guarantee inside a stopped process. A stopped process emits no
476	effects; on resume its first checkpoint or tick observes the stall and fail-
477	stops before any further effect.
478	
479	The observation predicate revokes on a higher counter whose entries name the
480	closure (release, signing key, namespace, catalog snapshot) or on a policy
481	digest change that removes a required grant; unrelated changes are recorded as
482	drift; a lower counter never revokes (rollback is detected by the floor rules).
483	
484	**Linearization** is under the single journal append lock: after `REV` no
485	`RA`, intent, commit or `SEAL` is appended, and no brokered effect commits.
486	Commit records carry `postimageSha256`. At `REV(trust-revoked)` the host
487	attempts rollback of reversible completed effects **only where the current
488	bytes equal the committed postimage**; a mismatch is `rollbackBlocked`
489	(user-modified since commit, never overwritten), an unreadable target is
490	`indeterminate`. Irreversible completed effects and effects under
491	`REV(policy|operator)` are disclosed as completed. The `CLN` record lists every
492	residual. Cancellation is bounded: refuse further requests (0 s), protocol
493	Cancel (2 s), SIGTERM (3 s), SIGKILL of the process group and reap (5 s),
494	scratch cleanup under the lease; total 10 s under the same qualification
495	standing. **Unconfined children** (repository code under S10) are not brokered
496	effects: they are cancelled within the bound and disclosed, and their external
497	effects before the kill are not enumerable. No confinement is claimed.
498	
499	**Three different SEAL boundaries, not one.** (1) `linearize` is an abstract
500	brokered-effect schedule over a grant journal. Its all-zero `run3:` SEAL id is
501	a **fixture** token for that schedule. It is not a product host, not native
502	fact authority, and not `identity-model.v3.close_run`. (2)
503	`admit_seal_run_id_prefix` is narrow `run3` pattern dispatch. It admits a
504	well-formed non-fixture prefix and refuses `run2` and the fixture id. It does
505	not replay a graph. (3) `admit_analysis_seal` is the public reference SEAL of
506	an analysis Run: current `JournalRecord` fields (`recordSchema` 3, closed
507	required members), then `identity-model.v3.close_run` on the supplied retained
508	graph, then byte-equal RunId comparison. Owner-only `open_run_closure` is not
509	that boundary. A well-formed `run3:` that is not the replayed identity refuses
510	`SEAL_RUN_ID_MISMATCH`. Schema-2 journals remain frozen historical bytes and
511	are not read as 3. Mixed prefixes refuse. There is no `run[23]` alternation.
512	Revocation still blocks schedule-SEAL after `REV`. Grant/root schema-2
513	documents are a different axis. This dispatch does not change lease modes,
514	lock order, or permission-truth-table effect values. Proof
515	`executionInputsDigest` is required by identity reconstruct; this unit does
516	not mint it.
517	
518	**Commit-admission gate (one atomic bit state).** `ADMITTED = 1`, `LATCHED = 2`: `0` is
519	preparing, `1` admitted, `2` latched before admission, `3` admitted then latched. Commit
520	admission is a compare-exchange `0 → 1`; the observer always fetch-ORs `2`, including
521	`1 → 3`, so a post-admission latch cannot be lost. No state resets during the attempt. A
522	successful gate mints one internal single-use permit for the already prepared commit and is
523	not a reusable grant for later effects. A latch winning at state `0` prevents the gate
524	entirely. State `3` does **not** revoke the already admitted attempt or relabel its outcome:
525	it records the latch and forbids further effect admission or retries. The observer bound
526	bounds admitting new effects; it cannot abort an in-flight syscall or rewrite its outcome. A
527	confirmed durable commit stays committed; an uncertain commit or barrier stays
528	durability-undetermined with its ExecutionId and no automatic write retry. The gate orders
529	admission only and is not the durability point.
530	
531	**`REV` after `SEAL` is not a refusal.** The linearization law above constrains one
532	direction only: after `REV` no `RA`, intent, commit or `SEAL` is appended. It does not follow
533	that a `REV` appearing later in sequence order refuses an earlier `SEAL`. Durable commitment
534	is established solely by the guarded evidence-ledger receipt and its private association. A
535	reader must not infer refusal from record order, and no member is added to the closed
536	schema-3 `JournalRecord` to carry that correlation: the private association and the
537	`AttemptCustodyV1` `executionId ↔ operationRef` mapping (identity §2) are its lawful home.
538	
539	**A receipt present before its attempt is settled is lawful.** Because the settle write is
540	ordered after the receipt write, every committing attempt passes through an interval in which
541	a valid joined receipt exists while the private attempt row is still `admitted`. That is not
542	a contradiction and not a custody condition: the receipt establishes historical commitment,
543	pending settlement is disclosed operationally, and no authority is revived. No writer may
544	reopen a stopped session merely to settle it; settlement is the separately authorized sweep.
545	
546	**Required delivery is a separate phase.** On any end path security returns a stopped
547	cleanup-only session. Required rendering and delivery draw no authority from it: they are a
548	read-and-materialise activity in `SHARED-READ` mode (S7), not a brokered effect. The handoff
549	is: cleanup `REV`/`CLN` through a fresh lawful level-3 then level-4 append while the stopped
550	session still holds the operation lease; release the lease; ordinary S7 end handoff; then a
551	new `SHARED-READ` phase over the committed snapshot. A latched attempt (state `2` or `3`)
552	starts no delivery phase and cannot reacquire authority that way; for state `3` the commit
553	stays committed with its RunId observable and the required delivery is reported failed
554	through the existing `DELIVERY.REQUIRED_FAILED` path. This is the **selected** law, not an
555	open choice.
556	
557	**Publication does not overwrite the workflow outcome.** A successful publication does not
558	force `success` at exit 0. A Run that publishes and then fails its policy assessment
559	terminates `policy-failed` at exit 1 carrying that committed `runId`; a Run whose verdict is
560	indeterminate terminates `indeterminate` at exit 3 carrying its `reasonCodes`. An optional
561	surface failure is disclosed without rewriting either, and `success` can carry neither an
562	`errorCode` nor `reasonCodes`, so no lawful reset to success exists. Required delivery
563	failure is the one lawful class change, and it preserves the RunId.
564	
565	**Carrier anchor bound (selected limit).** No current owner asserts cryptographic
566	authentication of the interior journal prefix. The v8 closed witness member `bodySha256`
567	names the tail body digest, so it detects no interior substitution, and the inherited chain
568	value binds only the immediately previous body digest and index. Confirming a retained
569	carrier therefore establishes presence, contiguity and non-rollback below the last observed
570	operation boundary, under the conclusion class `confirmed-under-retained-custody`. An unmet
571	anchor is reported unknown, never as invalidation. This is a selected compatibility and
572	security limit with a recorded disposition, not an open defect, and the historical v1 prose
573	noted in S1 is not a current claim to the contrary.
