575	## S7. Leases and lock order (AR-14)
576	
577	The current security schema bundle declares every array's `x-opensip-order`
578	under identity §3. Namespace lists use strictly unique raw UTF-8 locator order;
579	execution-grant owner records use strictly unique `ownerKey` order. Public code
580	sets use strictly unique UTF-8 order. Other arrays are explicit sequences unless
581	their owning schema states a stricter order: journal revisions, lock traces,
582	release steps, signature entries and observations are never silently sorted.
583	This collection-admission law does not change the security metadata canonical
584	profile or its immutable historical schemas.
585	
586	| Level | Lock | Carrier | Blocking |
587	|---|---|---|---|
588	| 0 | lifecycle fence | `<installRoot>/lifecycle.fence`, flock LOCK_EX | bounded wait 5 s, then `PROJECT.BUSY` |
589	| 1 | project writer lease | `<namespace>/writer.lease`, LOCK_EX\|LOCK_NB | never |
590	| 2 | project reader lease | `<namespace>/readers.lease`, LOCK_SH\|LOCK_NB (readers); LOCK_EX\|LOCK_NB (EXCLUSIVE) | never |
591	| 3 | ledger transaction | SQLite WAL; writers BEGIN IMMEDIATE, busy_timeout 0; readers read a committed snapshot | never for readers |
592	| 4 | journal append lock | in-process mutex | bounded, in-process |
593	
594	Modes: `SHARED-READ` (any number; queries, rendering, doctor, read-only
595	agents), `APPEND-WRITE` (one; analysis, import, baseline pin; publishes only
596	new immutable objects and ledger rows, never deletes or rewrites bytes a reader
597	may reference), `EXCLUSIVE` (GC, purge, migration, repair apply; nothing else
598	held). Readers never block a writer; a second writer or an EXCLUSIVE request
599	gets `PROJECT.BUSY` at once, releases the fence, and may retry outside the
600	fence with backoff 1/2/4/8/15 s within a 30 s budget. Laws: no lease without
601	the fence; no waiting for a lease; no waiting for the fence while holding a
602	lease (operation end releases the lease first); no upgrade; trust state is
603	written only under the fence and never under a lease; GC census is a
604	LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB probe under the fence and a busy probe means retain.
605	
606	**One-writer refinement (identity-and-evidence §5).** "Exactly one per-project
607	writer holds the lifecycle lease through admission, evaluation and commit" is
608	the APPEND-WRITE mode: exactly one append writer, coexisting with any number of
609	immutable-snapshot readers that never wait on it. The EXCLUSIVE mode is the
610	refinement for migration, purge, GC and repair apply, which need a reader
611	census (the LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB probe) because they may remove or rewrite bytes a
612	reader could reference. There is no contradiction with the identity contract:
613	readers are invisible to the writer's commit order and the writer is invisible
614	to readers' snapshots. Exact selectors: `<namespace>/writer.lease` LOCK_EX|NB
615	is the identity contract's "lifecycle lease"; `<namespace>/readers.lease`
616	LOCK_SH|NB is its "consistent committed snapshot"; `<installRoot>/lifecycle.fence`
617	is its "global trust admission and revocation lock order".
618	
619	**Namespaces.** Every project lease names a namespace from the host namespace
620	registry (ProjectId ↔ namespace locator, identity §5); a lease on an
621	unregistered namespace is a violation, never an implicit registration
622	(`lease-on-an-unregistered-namespace-is-refused-negative`). Namespaces are
623	independent: a writer in one never blocks a writer in another.
624	
625	**Core-transition lock set (decided; SHOULD-6).** `core update|repair|rollback`
626	and `store migrate|rollback` change install-level state, while EXCLUSIVE is a
627	per-namespace lease. The mechanism is a composition, not a new flock mode:
628	
629	1. The install-wide fence (level 0) is held for the **whole** transition, not
630	   only for lease acquisition; no project operation can be admitted meanwhile.
631	2. The affected namespace set is enumerated from the registry by
632	   `core_transition_affected_namespaces` (never from user input or a directory
633	   listing): **all registered namespaces** when the from/to state schema differ
634	   or a store is re-selected (`core rollback`, `store migrate|rollback`);
635	   **no namespace** for a same-schema `core update` or `core repair`, because
636	   the selected core closure is an immutable generation, running project
637	   operations keep their pinned generation and re-check trust at their S6
638	   checkpoints, and nothing they reference is rewritten.
639	3. EXCLUSIVE is taken on each affected namespace in namespace-locator byte
640	   order, non-blocking and all-or-nothing: the first busy namespace releases
641	   every acquired lease in reverse order, releases the fence, reports
642	   `PROJECT.BUSY` naming that namespace and its holders, and the retry is the
643	   ordinary backoff outside the fence.
644	4. The `InstallationTransitionJournalV1` (S9.2) names the exact lease set and is
645	   written only after every lease is held: in the lock model the
646	   `transition-journal` action is lawful only under the fence, only after
647	   `core-transition-acquire` succeeded, and only naming exactly the held set
648	   (`transition-journal-*` cases). Crash
649	   recovery runs as the first act under the next fence acquisition, before any
650	   admission, over the S9.2 recovery table (which defers to the S9 footprint
651	   table for store operations), and re-acquires exactly the journaled
652	   set; flock leases die with the process, so no stale lease survives. A
653	   namespace registered after the intent cannot exist (registration needs the
654	   fence); finding one is `MIGRATION.CORRUPT`.
655	5. Leases are released in reverse order, then the fence. The fence cannot be
656	   released while transition leases are held.
657	
658	Ordinary component `install`/`update` publish new immutable generations under
659	the fence alone and never revoke a generation a live operation pins (removal
660	is GC census only). GC iterates registered namespaces and treats a busy
661	namespace as retain, never as refusal. Reference `lease_schedule` (registry,
662	`core-transition-acquire|release`, `transition-journal`),
663	`core_transition_affected_namespaces`; cases `core-transition-*`,
664	`transition-journal-*`, `two-namespaces-are-independent-*`.
665	
666	Command → lease map (workflows command inventory):
667	
668	| Lease | Commands |
669	|---|---|
670	| none (fence only, no project lock) | `install`, `update` (component generations), `trust refresh|import|recovery-challenge|recovery-import`, ordinary payload import, `doctor` / `trust doctor` / `store status` (report-only, no write) |
671	| SHARED-READ | `query`, `recommend`, `baseline show`, `policy show|test`, `candidates`, `inspect`, `review brief`, `repair preview`, `agent serve` reads, `doctor` project checks |
672	| APPEND-WRITE | `opensip` default, `analyze`, `fit`, `audit`, `import`, `baseline adopt|export|upgrade`, `policy init`, `waive`, `review join`, `test run`, `native prepare`, `repair verify` |
673	| EXCLUSIVE (one namespace) | `repair apply` (S10.1 authorization), `repair recover --apply-recovery` (S10.2 authorization; inspection alone is SHARED-READ), `purge`, `store gc` per namespace (busy = retain) |
674	| core-transition lock set (fence held + EXCLUSIVE on every affected registered namespace) | `core update`, `core repair`, `core rollback`, `store migrate`, `store rollback` |
675	
676	Trust recovery deliberately takes no project lease: it mutates SC-TRUST only,
677	under the fence, and a project operation that starts afterwards observes the
678	new floor at its trust instant.

731	## S9. Stage transition, schema bridge and floor continuity (AR-14)
732	
733	Bridge. Stage 1: root readers {1}, state decoder v1, TR-REPAIR typed absence,
734	`kernelAttestationKeys` empty. Stage 2: root readers {1, 2}, state decoders
735	`state-decoder.v1` (read-only migration source) and `state-decoder.v2`
736	(writer); schema-2 roots may carry an active TR-REPAIR (threshold ≥ 2, keys ≥
737	threshold + 1, namespaces present, no reuse of root keys) and up to 8 kernel
738	attestation keys (no reuse of root keys). Ordered release: (1) the stage-2 core
739	ships under the schema-1 catalog, so every stage-1 install updates by its
740	ordinary path; (2) root N+1 with schema 2 is signed by root-N keys and its own
741	keys; (3) stage-1 cores refuse N+1 typed and keep N until it expires; stage-2
742	cores accept it by the dual reader; (4) state migration 1→2 runs under
743	EXCLUSIVE. Both stages keep the metadata profile of S2.
744	
745	**Physical carrier bridge (carrierFormat).** The project grant-journal carrier has its
746	own format axis, and it is not the state schema. Detection on open is by schema
747	introspection only, because the oldest format carries no version row: object names
748	first, then refusal on a partial set, then definition validation, and the published
749	`carrier_format` row read **last**. Reader staging mirrors the root-reader and
750	state-decoder pattern, and its scope is stated precisely: a **carrierFormat-aware** core
751	that supports only {1, 2} refuses a carrierFormat 3 carrier **typed** and keeps its prior
752	generation until it expires; a carrierFormat {1, 2, 3} core reads both, under
753	recordSchema-1 semantics for historical generations and recordSchema-3 for current ones.
754	A **format-unaware** core cannot be made to refuse at all, because it never looks for
755	`carrier_format`; that limitation is selected and disclosed, detectable but not
756	preventable, and a generation at or above `first_generation` appearing in the inherited
757	table is a split-brain custody condition, never valid history. Its mitigation is the
758	existing ordered-release discipline. A historical `platform` value is surfaced as a
759	historical alias and is never presented as an S8 machine id, rewritten, or joined to
760	`RepoExecutionGrantV2.platformId`. An unmigrated carrier stays fully READABLE for its
761	existing generations, but it cannot admit a schema-3 `SEAL`, so an attempt needing to
762	seal there refuses with the carrier-incompatibility standing until migration completes.
763	
764	**Carrier migration is NOT an installation transition.** It does not use the S9.2 intent
765	or journal, and it cannot: reusing the closed logical `store-migrate` intent with an
766	unchanged state schema and store generation refuses
767	`TRANSITION.MIGRATE_REQUIRES_SCHEMA_ADVANCE` and
768	`TRANSITION.SCHEMA_CHANGE_SELECTS_NEW_STORE`, and an invented `carrier-migrate` operation
769	refuses `TRANSITION.OPERATION`. `InstallationTransitionIntentV1` is a closed 11-member
770	record and `InstallationTransitionJournalV1` a closed 20-member record; neither has a
771	carrier field. Migration 1 or 2 → 3 is instead a **selected prospective expansion** of
772	the existing `store-gc` operation (security-owned, `authorizationClass:
773	exclusive-lease`, `writesTrackedIntent: false`): the inherited row shows only that
774	`store-gc` is not an intent-writing transition, not that this mutation was already
775	authorized, so the added per-namespace behaviour is selected here explicitly. It runs
776	under the install fence with non-blocking `EXCLUSIVE` on
777	the affected project namespace, where a busy namespace is skipped and retained exactly as
778	GC already behaves. Its state is reported through the existing `store-status`
779	`migration-state` field. It is additive, disables no inherited constraint or trigger, and
780	rewrites no inherited row. Three atomic durable acts in order — `TERMINAL` append, object
781	creation, format-row publication — with the format ROW as the commit point and detection
782	keyed on that row, so every durable prefix has an exact resume action. Protocol:
783	`design-corrections/security/carrier-migration.v1.md`. A format-unaware core cannot be
784	made to refuse a migrated carrier, so a generation at or above `first_generation`
785	appearing in the inherited table is a detectable split-brain custody condition, never
786	valid history; the mitigation is the existing ordered-release pattern.
787	
788	**Grant-generation closure gains a third cause.** The inherited rule (security v8 §5.4
789	WA-13, retained unchanged as historical text) advances `grantGeneration` only on
790	whole-generation `REV` and on the uint53 rollover. Carrier-format migration is a third
791	cause of generation closure. It reuses the existing typed `TERMINAL` cause
792	`grantGenerationClosure` and changes no schema, enum or wire major. Floors copy forward
793	unchanged and a poisoned floor is not lowered; only S4.5 lowers it.
794	
795	Migration writes a `migrating` root: PREPARING → PREPARED → (old store fenced
796	`RESTORED`) → COMMITTED → final rename. Recovery from the durable footprint
797	only: absent = nothing to do; PREPARING or PREPARED with the old store unfenced
798	= abort; PREPARED with the old store fenced = resume from step 3; COMMITTED =
799	resume the final rename; final and migrating coexisting, or unknown state =
800	quarantine `MIGRATION.CORRUPT`. Floors (`rootVersion`, `indexSnapshotVersion`,
801	`revocationVersion`, `evalHighWater`, `lastAccepted`, `recoveryEpochSerial`)

803	not; roles re-establish by the PRESENT event over the embedded chain. A new core

805	`ROOT.FLOOR_ABOVE_CORE`. Rollback inside the 30 d window re-selects the retained

953	### S9.3 Private store-instance lineage (successor; proposed, not accepted)
954	
955	A numeric store generation is not unique over time: `store-rollback` re-selects a
956	retained generation and `core-rollback` never raises the schema, so two physically
957	distinct stores can present the same `(storeGeneration, stateSchema)` pair. A
958	private **store instance identity** disambiguates them for local operational
959	records. It adds no member to `InstallationTransitionIntentV1`,
960	`InstallationTransitionJournalV1`, the namespace registry or any signed document,
961	introduces no envelope kind and no public major, and mints no D9 class, code or
962	exit; its refusals are the existing `TRANSITION.*` set and the existing
963	`MIGRATION.CORRUPT` quarantine. It is never a wire field, an authority token or a
964	semantic input, and it never enters the pure evaluator or a Run hash.
965	
966	**Instance identity.** Each physical store instance carries one `storeInstanceId`:
967	32 lowercase hexadecimal characters from 128 bits of OS CSPRNG, allocated once
968	when that store is created, persisted in that store's own root before the store is
969	first published, and never rewritten. It has no ordering and no arithmetic, and
970	reading it grants nothing.
971	
972	**Lineage nodes, identified by the full triple.** A private append-only table
973	holds one node per admitted binding triple
974	`(storeInstanceId, storeGeneration, stateSchema)`, carrying its predecessor triple
975	and the `intentDigest` of the transition that created it; both are `null` exactly
976	at a **lineage root**. Every lookup uses the whole triple, whose instance component
977	is read from the store-root **marker** of the store concerned: a numeric pair alone
978	never identifies a node, because a retained branch may lawfully present the same
979	pair as a fresh target. `intentDigest` is evidence validated *on* the selected node

980	and is never a search key, since it may lawfully repeat. This section asserts no
981	global uniqueness of a store generation beyond what the rules above already impose.
982	
983	**Marker observation is three-way and phase-bound.** Reading a store root yields
984	exactly one of: a **readable** identity; **absent**, meaning no store root is
985	present; or **unreadable**, meaning a root was observed but its marker is missing
986	or malformed. An unreadable marker is never treated as absence, and an absence must
987	be observed, never inferred from a missing observation. The store a transition
988	comes from always exists, so its marker is always required. The **selected**
989	store's marker is required only where the transition is settled as committed: at
990	`LEASED` and `PREPARING` a forward selection's target may not yet be materialised,
991	and after an abort an unpublished target may already have been reclaimed by the GC
992	census, so an absent target there is expected and must never be read as corruption.
993	
994	**One admission law.** A node is admitted only if its shape is admitted by the
995	private record's own closed schema, its predecessor and origin digest are null
996	together or present together, it does not name its own triple, its non-null
997	predecessor already exists as a node at that exact triple, no existing node shares
998	its primary key with disagreeing contents, and the chain from it is acyclic and
999	reaches exactly **one** lineage root. That root rule is scoped to the chain, not to
1000	the whole table: an authorized restore or adoption starts its own lineage, so
1001	several lineages may coexist. Publication and recovery apply this same law, and an
1002	exact byte-identical match at the target key is idempotent but **not** a short
1003	circuit — it is validated the same way and simply writes nothing. A refusal writes
1004	nothing.
1005	
1006	**Selection case, derived from the admitted intent alone.** By the pair law in
1007	S9.2 the case is decidable without reading any stored node: equal `to`/`from`
1008	generation and schema is a **same-store** selection; an advanced schema is a
1009	**forward selection**; a retreated schema is an **ancestor re-selection**. Only a
1010	forward selection materialises a new store, allocates a fresh `storeInstanceId`
1011	and writes one node, after the journal record is durably `COMMITTED` and never
1012	inside a level-4 grant-journal append lock. A same-store or ancestor re-selection
1013	writes no node: the store it selects already has one, created by an earlier act.
1014	
1015	**Recovery applies the same case, and only after the owner decides.**
1016	`recover_transition_journal` keeps every decision it already makes; this adds no
1017	state, code or recovery action, and in particular a core operation at `PREPARED`
1018	still aborts and a store operation still follows the S9 footprint. Where that
1019	function refuses, reports the project busy or quarantines, the companion makes **no
1020	decision at all**, inspects nothing and reads no marker. Where its action settles
1021	the transition as committed — `RESUME-COMMIT` or `RELEASE-ONLY` reaching `DONE` —
1022	then: a **forward selection** node must be present at its own full triple, or else
1023	reconstructed from the journal record's own from/to generation and schema members
1024	together with the predecessor and selected store-root markers, and admitted by the
1025	law above. A **same-store or ancestor** re-selection validates the retained node at
1026	its own full triple and **never rewrites its predecessor or origin digest**; an
1027	ancestor must additionally lie on the verified chain from the current node, so a
1028	store at a merely equal numeric pair off that chain never qualifies. That node was
1029	created by an earlier, unrelated act whose origin the current intent does not carry,
1030	so a missing one cannot be repaired from it and is `QUARANTINE` /
1031	`MIGRATION.CORRUPT`. No atomicity is claimed between the journal record and a node.
1032	
1033	**Before the owner settles a transition**, pre-existing ancestry is expected and
1034	untouched, including a retained branch at the same numeric generation, and an
1035	absent target is expected as above. Where a target *is* observable, what must not
1036	exist is a *new* node for that transition at **its own full triple**. For a forward
1037	selection, any node at that new target triple is premature. For a same-store or
1038	ancestor re-selection, the pre-existing node is expected; only a node claiming the
1039	current unrelated transition as its origin is contradictory. Each is a premature-node contradiction
1040	and quarantines; ordinary pre-existing lineage remains unchanged.
1041	
1042	**Lineage roots.** A root is created by an authorized local act that materialises a
1043	new physical store outside any transition: installation, or an authorized evidence
1044	restore or portable adoption. Such an act allocates a fresh `storeInstanceId`,
1045	**replaces** any marker present in copied bytes before first publication so a
1046	restored store never impersonates its source, imports no node from the source, and
1047	imports no floor, grant or local commit authority. No transition is invented to
1048	give it an `intentDigest`.
1049	
1050	**Floors and authority are unchanged by this section.** An authorized transition
1051	keeps the S9 floor rules exactly: migration copies the floors forward into the new
1052	store, rollback inside the window sets them to the maximum of both stores, and a
1053	poisoned floor is lowered only by S4.5. An instance identity records which physical
1054	store is selected; it never lowers a floor and never confers local commit authority.

The new product's default authoritative analysis remains the explicitly invoked, disclosed first-write operation of identity §5. Distribution migration never invokes that operation implicitly.
1522	3. **Per-value provenance:** supported legacy projection records sourceSchemaVersion=1 and the original carrier/value origin; explicit new choices retain their own provenance. A default or migration cannot be reported as a tracked user choice.
1523	4. **Historical identities/custody:** original ids, bytes, evidence meaning, retention and ownership remain in the original custody account. No new product identity replaces, upgrades or retroactively authenticates a historical one; new source/Plan/Run identities are explicitly new-major identities. Coexistence does not erase historical review standing.
1524	5. **Promised offline behavior:** already installed prototype assets remain usable under their original promise. The new product's authoritative offline promise applies only to its separately admitted complete signed closure, including verified storage. Missing current assets cause typed unavailability/refusal, never an automatic download or fallback.
1525	
1526	All five distinctions remain explicit: (1) distribution migration selects executable generations; user-custody state migration is a separately authorized operation, and no prototype-state conversion is provided; (2) management-only adoption supplies management functions, while an authoritative closure additionally supplies every admitted executable/data/storage dependency; (3) immutable coexistence retains separately selected generations/installations, while in-place package mutation is forbidden; (4) removal drops installation/reference selection, while explicit purge alone changes retained evidence availability under identity §5; (5) replay pinning retains the exact runnable detector/evidence closure, while contract-approved typed degradation reports missing/expired/purged evidence without rewriting assurance or fabricating replay.
1527	
1528	Authoritative cache and regeneration hits inherit identity §4. Admission against a current Run is `identity-model.v3.close_run` complete evaluator3 semantic replay, then `admit_cache_entry` through that Run's own closure. Constructing `cache2` / `regen2` or matching a hash is not authority. `identity-model.py.close_run` of a `run2` graph is historical owner-closure admission (exact schema, identity, and native owner joins). It is not merely a hash compare, and it is not evaluator3 semantic replay. Expired or revoked permission cannot be resurrected by a matching hash. Installation recovery already requires reconstructing and admitting the retained transition intent over the frozen registry; a hash alone cannot authenticate a lawful scope. Retained historical `run2` custody stays those bytes.
1529	
1530	The six “No migration silently…” prohibitions are retained individually: no silent **download**, **index refresh**, **lock mutation**, **replacement historical identity**, **evidence-meaning rewrite**, or **telemetry/network requirement**. Explicit commands retain their separate consent, signed-input, expiry/revocation, custody, recovery and output laws. No migration authority is inferred from the mere presence of old data.
1531	
1532	Release owners must exercise the coexistence/foreign-root/legacy-config/no-write/offline/removal-versus-purge/replay-degradation positive and negative corpus at G06/G07/G11/G12/G18/G19/G21, with prototype baseline provenance and actual current product measurements. These are required implementation/release tests, not a claim that this design reference has executed the prototype or converted a database.
1533

75	
76	## 1. Invocation, step, attempt, Run (AR-08)
77	
78	An invocation is one host request. Its operational identity is `RequestId`, minted
79	before admission and retained for refusal as well as success. The invocation is an
80	ordered acyclic list of at most **64 steps**; `StepId` is the zero-based position.
81	Each admitted attempt of a step receives a fresh `ExecutionId`; a step has at most
82	**3 attempts**. Only `analysis` and `verify` steps seal or link a content-derived
83	`run3`. `comparison`, `query`, `render`, `import`, `repair-preview`, `repair-apply`,
84	`test-execution`, `native-preparation`, `mutation`, `export-delivery` and `doctor` are operational steps
85	that never mint a Run. Schema: `workflows/schemas/evaluator3/invocation-record.schema.json`.
86	
87	**Step DAG versus derivation DAG.** The step list is the operational workflow. Each
88	analysis/verify *attempt* owns exactly one derivation DAG (`exec-plan2`, at most
89	**1024 stages**) recorded in the attempt's `derivation` binding
90	(`planId`, `executionPlanId`, `stageCount`, `stagesCompleted`, `firstFailedStage`).
91	A step never depends on a stage and a stage never references a step. A retry on
92	identical admitted inputs may bind the same `exec-plan2` and the same Run; attempts
93	remain separately auditable.
94	
95	**Dependencies.** `dependsOn` names lower StepIds only (a forward or self reference is
96	`WORKFLOW.DEPENDENCY_CYCLE`, request-rejected). `requirement` is `required` or
97	`optional`; a required step may not depend on an optional step
98	(`WORKFLOW.REQUIRED_DEPENDS_ON_OPTIONAL`). `dependencyGate` is `completed` (every
99	dependency completed) or `terminal` (every dependency reached any terminal outcome;
100	lawful only for `render`/`export-delivery`, which project whatever happened). A
101	step whose gate is unmet is `skipped` with a typed `skipReason`. Step outcomes are
102	closed: `completed`, `rejected`, `failed`, `skipped`, `cancelled`, `abandoned`
103	(crash recovery only).
104	
105	**Retries.** `retryPolicy=idempotent-retry` is lawful only for `analysis`, `verify`,
106	`query`, `render`, `doctor` and `export-delivery`, only for `faultCause=ledger-busy`,
107	and within the 3-attempt budget; exhausting it is `LEDGER.BUSY_TIMEOUT` (4) with
108	detail `WORKFLOW.RETRY_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED`. `host-io` and every other fault are never
109	retried. `mutation`, `import`, `repair-preview`, `repair-apply`, `comparison`, `native-preparation` and `test-execution`
110	carry `retryPolicy=none` by schema; a spec violating this is refused.
111	
112	**Mutation idempotence and recovery.** Generic `mutation` steps use the bare
113	64-hex `H("workflow.mutation-intent", MutationReplayScopeV1)`. The closed retained
114	scope is exactly `{schemaVersion:1,requestId,stepId,projectId,operation}`, with
115	`operation` equal to `MutationParams.mutationClass`. This explicitly succeeds the
116	former undefined `{operation,projectId,effect preimage}` description. The key is
117	operational and scoped to one host-minted request and admitted immutable step;
118	different fresh requests never deduplicate each other's generic mutations.
119	`sourceStep` resolves inside that same retained invocation, whose admitted
120	parameters and completed dependency results are immutable. Before lookup or
121	replay the host validates the scope and full params, recomputes the key and
122	requires the retained invocation/project/step/operation binding; a caller cannot
123	nominate another invocation's scope or change effect inputs under an old key.
124	Receipt lookup is never an effect-authorization mechanism. A same-scope COMPLETED
125	receipt permits delivery replay with no second effect. Failure, unknown state or
126	incomplete execution requires the operation's existing recovery law, not blind
127	re-execution. Recovery started in a new request retains its own operational scope
128	and the explicit original journal/intent links required by §§6/12.
129	
130	**What a step's required receipt carries is published, not inferred.**
131	`MutationReceiptV1` **requires** both `operation` and `idempotencyKey`, and
132	`ImportResult` and `NativePreparationResult` both **require** a `receiptId`. The
133	owning domain for those branches is `workflow.mutation-receipt` — the **mutation**
134	receipt domain, not the only `receipt2:` one, since §10 also lists
135	`workflow.verification-link`. So an import step and a native-preparation step each
136	already owe a receipt carrying **both** required fields, and what was missing was
137	the binding for each. The operation binding is published as
138	`repair.schema.json#/x-opensip-mutation-operation-map/byStepKindReceiptOperation`,
139	beside the enum, and it is a deterministic function of the **step kind**:
140	
141	| Step kind | Receipt operation | Also carried in a request field? |
142	|---|---|---|
143	| `mutation` | the command's row in `byCommandGenericMutationStep` | yes — `MutationParams.mutationClass`, equal to `MutationReplayScopeV1.operation` |
144	| `repair-apply` | `repair-apply` | no — dedicated step, refused in both generic fields |
145	| `import` | `import` | no — `ImportParams`; §4's import receipt |
146	| `native-preparation` | `native-preparation` | no — `NativePreparationParams`; native §14's execution receipt |
147	
148	Because the binding is by **step kind and not by request class**, the `import`
149	step of the `analyze` command carries the same operation as the `import`
150	command's. That is also a worked case of **one operation emitted by two
151	commands**, which is why this map is *not* an inverse map and must not be read
152	backwards. A command with none of these four step kinds mints no operation.
153	
154	**The idempotency key is bound too, and sharing a recipe is not sharing replay
155	authority.** `receiptIdempotencyKeyByStepKind` publishes, per step kind, the exact
156	deterministic preimage and the *lookup meaning* separately:
157	
158	| Step kind | Key | Lookup meaning |
159	|---|---|---|
160	| `mutation` | `H("workflow.mutation-intent", MutationReplayScopeV1)` | equal COMPLETED receipt permits delivery replay with no second effect |
161	| `repair-apply` | raw SHA-256 of `C({operation, projectId, repairPlanId, baseSnapshotId})` | equal completed key performs no second effect |
162	| `import` | the same H over the closed scope with `operation: "import"` | **delivery only**, within the same retained invocation; never a cross-request dedupe |
163	| `native-preparation` | the same H with `operation: "native-preparation"` | **not replay**: it identifies that step's receipt and authorizes nothing |
164	
165	No new H domain, record or authority is introduced: `MutationReplayScopeV1.operation`
166	**already admits** both tokens — they are two of the 23 — which is a further reason
167	that domain stays wider than the current generic emitters. The user-supplied import
168	path is deliberately **not** in the preimage, because §4 keeps it out of identity
169	entirely. The receipt key is operational and already contains `RequestId`.
170	`ExecutionId` stays out because this key is scoped to one admitted invocation and
171	step; each attempt keeps its separate `ExecutionId`. These immutable bindings
172	grant no execution or retry authority.
173	
174	**The three non-generic kinds are still not generic replay.** They carry their own
175	params rather than `MutationParams`, are not generic `mutation` steps, and carry
176	`retryPolicy=none` by schema. Import custody, mandatory source correspondence and
177	the staleness disposition are unchanged and re-checked — a receipt substitutes for
178	none of them. A fresh native preparation is a **new explicit authorized execution**
179	under its own `AuthorizedExecutionV2` and grant set with **no automatic retry**; a
180	completed receipt never suppresses one, and this binding grants no permission the
181	security unit does not already admit.
182	
183	Across these step kinds, **four** commands do not share their operation's name,
184	so the operation cannot be derived by name matching. Three use generic mutation steps:
185	`baseline-upgrade` → `baseline-upgrade-apply` (the operation names the apply
186	half; the analysis half mints a Run, not a mutation), `policy-init` →
187	`policy-write` and `waive` → `waiver-change` (both are effect classes covering
188	more than the one command spelling). The fourth is the execution-class
189	`native-prepare` → `native-preparation`, whose operation is carried by its own
190	step kind; it is published with the other three because counting only the
191	mutation-class commands would leave one command's operation still underivable.
192	The published set is held **equal** to the commands whose name is not itself a
193	`MutationOperation` member, so a later rename cannot be added to the vocabulary
194	without appearing here. Two further facts are disclosed rather than tidied away:
195	`repair-apply` is bound by its own step kind, and being in the map does **not**
196	make it admissible in either generic position — both still refuse it by schema;
197	and `config-write` is the one `MutationOperation` member that **no step kind binds
198	and no command in this inventory emits**, which is stated rather than removed or
199	given an invented command, and which stays admissible in the generic field because
200	narrowing a generic domain to today's emitters would remove a value no finding
201	asked to remove. Publishing the map adds no command, no operation, no receipt and
202	no accepted request. What the reference model in this kit does **not** do is emit
203	an import or native-preparation receipt; that is a stated qualification limit of
204	the reference evidence and is deliberately distinct from the design law above.
205	
206	Repair apply is the explicit content-derived exception: it is a dedicated
207	`repair-apply` step, excluded from generic MutationParams. It uses the raw SHA-256 of
208	canonical `{operation:"repair-apply",projectId,repairPlanId,baseSnapshotId}` as its
209	idempotency key. An equal completed key performs no second effect. The original
210	receipt is immutable; a replay delivery produces a separately identified receipt
211	with the new request/attempt binding and `replayed=true`. Mutation receipts use
212	`receipt2:` plus `H('workflow.mutation-receipt', receiptWithoutReceiptId)` and remain
213	retained when an effect or later verification fails. Read-only recovery inspection
214	is distinct from separately authorized recovery writes (§6).
215	
216	**Audit gate ownership.** An analysis step declares `verdictGate=self|delegated`.
217	`self` applies its Run verdict. `delegated` requires authoritative analysis and a
218	consuming comparison step: a completed failing Run then contributes operational
219	success with its RunId, while the comparison owns the regression gate. This lets
220	inherited findings remain visible without failing the PR. Missing required Coverage
221	still contributes indeterminate; delegation cannot hide an incomplete analysis.
222	The comparison result is a distinct closed `ComparisonStepResult`, never a Run.
223	
224	**Cancellation.** A signal is recorded with the phase at which it arrived.
225	*before-settle* (some required step not yet terminal): remaining steps are
226	`cancelled`, the aggregate is `interrupted` (130), and a Run committed by an earlier
227	step is named in the termination's `runId`. *after-settle* (every required step
228	already terminal): the aggregate is **not reclassified**; the settled class stands.
229	Per kind: an analysis attempt aborts and leaves no Run; an import discards its
230	staged bytes; a repair-apply honours cancellation only before `APPLYING`, and during
231	the bounded rename loop the journal, not the signal, decides (§6).
232	
233	**Aggregate termination (D9 ordering preserved).** Over required steps only:
234	`operational-failed` > `request-rejected` > `policy-failed` > `indeterminate` >
235	`success`. An optional step's rejection or failure never changes the aggregate.
236	Policy fail dominates indeterminate across steps exactly as inside one Run, and a
237	required operational fault dominates a committed failing Run (its `runId` is still
238	carried). Exit code derives from class by the fixed table only. Ties retain the first
239	termination carrying domain detail in step order, or the first termination when
240	none carries detail, so a useful comparison remedy is preserved.
241	
242	**Ephemeral analysis.** `--ephemeral` produces the second member of the closed
243	`AnalysisResult` union: `authority=ephemeral`, `durability=not-required`, no `runId`,
244	no receipt, only semantic `planId`/`evidenceId` so the result can be cited. It cannot
245	satisfy baseline adoption, repair preview/apply, verify or authoritative replay
246	(`WORKFLOW.EPHEMERAL_CANNOT_SUPPLY_AUTHORITY`, `REQUEST.UNSATISFIABLE`, exit 2). A
247	failing ephemeral verdict terminates `policy-failed` with `authority=ephemeral`
248	instead of a `runId`; the branch contract admits exactly one of the two.
249	
250	**Default invocation.** `opensip` with no arguments is discovery then one durable
251	authoritative analysis (steps `analysis`, `render`). Retention is DEFAULTED
252	durable-unbounded (CD-RT-5), disclosed with the storage root before first write.
253	No policy file is written implicitly.
254	
255	---
256	
257	## 2. Portable baseline and runnable prior detector (AR-10)
258	
259	The major2 baseline artifact lives in the repository as tracked intent
260	(`opensip.baseline.json`). `baselineId = H('workflow.baseline', descriptor)`. The
261	descriptor pins: origin ProjectId, source `snapshot2`, the **authoritative** `run3`
262	and `plan2` (an ephemeral result is refused: `BASELINE.SOURCE_EPHEMERAL`), the
263	fingerprint recipe (`finding-fingerprint`, major ≥ 2), every contributing detector's
264	`closure2` with semantics major, the complete **pivot closure** (detector executable,
265	evaluator, provider, toolchain/stdlib, schema set; each a `closure2` with manifest digest,
266	protocol major and platform), the evaluation context digests, the **embedded**
267	policy/scope/waiver documents whose digests equal those context digests, rule
268	coverage (including each rule's recorded absence knowledge, §3), sorted unique matched entries and explicit unmatched occurrences.
269	Matched occurrences group only after equal fingerprint preimages and agreement
270	on every BaselineEntry field. Messages, parameters and citations remain on each
271	original finding. Unmatched findings retain their finding and subject identities;
272	they cannot be silently discarded or assigned a guessed stable fingerprint.
273	Custody (outside identity) carries host release,
274	export time, `retentionPins` (the Run and every pivot closure) and an optional signed
275	`closureBundle` reference.
276	
277	**Detector identity.** A detector is identified by its evaluator emission contribution.
278	`detectorClosure` has exactly one row per distinct `contributionId` of the origin Plan's
279	`EvaluatorEmissionPlanV1` rule rows, disabled rules included: `detectorId` equals that
280	`contributionId`, and `closureId` and `semanticsMajor` are that row's `detectorClosure` and
281	`semanticsMajor`, which equal the policy rule's `ruleProgramRef` major. Two rows for one
282	contribution with a different closure or major refuse (`CONFIG.INVALID` /
283	`EVALUATION.FINDING_JOIN_REFUSED`). `BaselineEntry.detectorId` is the `contributionId` of the
284	entry rule's emission binding and is a member of `detectorClosure`; comparison `detectorId`
285	values use the same identity. Baseline admission checks these joins after recomputing
286	`baselineId`, so a self-consistently reminted rename of a detector identity is refused rather
287	than accepted as a different baseline.
288	
289	**Fresh CI.** Comparison never reads the origin machine's store. A fresh host admits
290	the artifact by recomputing `baselineId`, checking schema major, recipe major,
291	sortedness, context-document digests and project correspondence (same ProjectId, or
292	explicit `--accept-origin`, else `BASELINE.PROJECT_UNMAPPED` and no comparison). It
293	resolves each pivot closure from (a) a retained generation, (b) an installed signed
294	release with the same `closure2`, or (c) the signed closure bundle; all under
295	**current trust**. A closure that is missing (`pivot-detector-unavailable`), revoked
296	(`pivot-closure-revoked`) or incompatible with the host's protocol majors/platform
297	(`pivot-closure-incompatible`) makes E0 unavailable; a revoked closure is never
298	executed, whatever bytes are present.
299	
300	**Detector semantics.** Semantics can change within a major, so two-way comparison

300	**Detector semantics.** Semantics can change within a major, so two-way comparison
301	is lawful only when the closures are identical (`identical-closure`) or the current
302	detector's authenticated compatibility listing names the baseline `closure2` as
303	exactly semantically compatible at the same major (`declared-compatible`).
304	Security S1 binds this optional listing to the unique regular-file path
305	`.opensip/detector-compatibility.json` in the already admitted same `closure2`
306	tree. The listing uses `schemas/evaluator3/detector-manifest.schema.json`;
307	its exact retained byte length and SHA256 must match the signed tree file.
308	`closure.manifestDigest` continues to identify the component manifest body.
309	An absent reserved path means no declaration; a valid empty listing declares
310	no compatible peers; a present invalid, non-file or unavailable listing refuses
311	(`REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED` / `EVALUATION.PROJECTION_INPUT_INCOMPLETE`; the refusal
312	message is diagnostic only) and cannot silently become absence. The host admission origin is one of the
313	three current-trust paths above. Caller-provided compatibility or trust claims
314	do not supply that admission. Otherwise the baseline detector
315	must run over current source (`three-way-pivot`, an authoritative pivot analysis step
316	planned before the primary one) or the detector's entries are `INDETERMINATE`.
317	Fingerprint dual emission (`legacyFingerprint`) migrates identity only and never
318	supplies the prior algorithm. Adoption pins the Run and the pivot closures as
319	retention roots; loss of a pin is disclosed as partial availability and yields typed
320	indeterminacy, never a silent two-way fallback. `baseline-upgrade` re-adopts under the
321	current detector explicitly and is a mutation with its own receipt.
322	
323	**Baseline show.** `opensip baseline show [PATH]` admits the tracked artifact as above and reports,
324	for each descriptor pivot closure in order, its current-trust state: `missing` (no admitted record
325	or bytes), `revoked` (trust not admitted), `incompatible` (unsupported protocol major, or a platform
326	that is neither the host's nor `any`), or `available` with its trust origin (retained generation,
327	installed signed release or signed closure bundle). These states are data, not a failure.

331	## 3. Multi-axis comparison (AR-11)
332	
333	The major2 comparison result (`comparison2:` = `H('workflow.comparison', descriptor)`)
334	attributes every fingerprint to the **first** axis at which it changes along a fixed
335	counterfactual chain evaluated over *current* source:
336	
337	| Pivot | Facts from | Policy | Scope | Waivers |
338	|---|---|---|---|---|
339	| B | baseline artifact entries | prior | prior | prior |
340	| E0 | prior detector closure over current source | prior | prior | prior |
341	| E1 | current detector | prior | prior | prior |
342	| E2 | current detector | current | prior | prior |
343	| E3 | current detector | current | current | prior |
344	| E4 | current Run | current | current | current |
345	
346	Axis order is code (B→E0), detection (E0→E1), policy (E1→E2), scope (E2→E3),
347	waiver (E3→E4, by waived status). E1–E3 are pure re-evaluations of retained current
348	facts under the baseline's embedded documents. They are available only when their
349	results were actually bound; an unchanged axis is `not-needed`, and a required
350	unbound re-evaluation is `unavailable` with typed indeterminacy. E0 is
351	`not-needed` when the detector is unchanged or declared compatible, `available`
352	when the pivot ran, `unavailable` otherwise. Classifications are `UNCHANGED`,
353	`CODE-NET-NEW`, `CODE-FIXED`, `DETECTION-DELTA`, `POLICY-DELTA`, `SCOPE-DELTA`,
354	`WAIVER-DELTA`, `EVIDENCE-DELTA`, `INDETERMINATE`; each entry also records
355	`presence` at every pivot and `subsequentDeltas` (later axes at which it changed
356	again). Deleting a waiver while adding a bug therefore yields one `WAIVER-DELTA` and
357	one `CODE-NET-NEW`; a bug introduced and simultaneously hidden by disabling the rule
358	is `CODE-NET-NEW` with `subsequentDeltas=[policy]`.
359	
360	**Evidence for presence.** The fingerprint population is the union of B and
361	all admitted E0–E4 results, including fingerprints present only in a pivot.
362	A known matched finding establishes presence even when waived; waiver status
363	is a separate axis. Absence of a particular fingerprint requires complete
364	subject enumeration, determinate `emitWhen` proof roots for every selected
365	subject, and that fingerprint absent from the exact admitted emission set.
366	A known finding on another subject does not invalidate this negative knowledge.
367	All-false roots establish the stronger claim that the rule emitted no findings.
368	Required execution deficiencies still affect the overall Run and comparison
369	verdict; they do not retract a determinate per-rule fingerprint result.
370	An advisory `pass` alone does not establish absence. A false root may retain
371	unknown child witnesses under the published three-valued composition law;
372	those witnesses do not turn a determinate false root into unknown. Unknown
373	roots, incomplete enumeration, disabled evaluation and exhausted budgets do
374	not establish a negative result. Known hits remain usable in a partial result.
375	
376	**One presence-knowledge law on every side.** B, E0–E3 and E4 are each `true` (a known
377	matched occurrence), `false` or `null` (not known). `false` is either non-selection or
378	evaluated absence. Non-selection holds when that side's own policy does not enable the rule or
379	its ScopeDocument does not select the path: the side cannot emit the fingerprint, so the change
380	is attributed to the policy or scope axis that removed the selection. It is not an evaluated
381	negative result, and because B, E0 and E1 share the baseline selection it never becomes
382	`CODE-FIXED`. Evaluated absence is proved under the law above for that side's rule, including
383	the attested path extent and correspondence knowledge: an unmatched occurrence of the same rule
384	that might be the fingerprint leaves that side's presence `null`, because complete enumeration
385	with such an occurrence is not proof the fingerprint was fixed or never present. Such an
386	occurrence is related unless the paths differ or its retained subject kind, language and
387	qualified name provably differ from the fingerprint's subject key; where no stronger relation is
388	retained, the same-rule/same-path barrier applies. No fingerprint is ever minted for an unmatched
389	occurrence, and a known matched hit stays `true`. The absence of a matched current hit is not by itself a known
390	`false`: for an enabled rule selecting the path, incomplete or unknown enumeration, unknown
391	roots and an exhausted budget leave E4 `null`. B is evaluated-absent for a non-entry only when
392	the baseline's `RuleCoverage.absenceKnowledge` for that rule is `complete-hit-set`, recorded at
393	adoption by the same law and no retained baseline `unmatchedOccurrences` row has the same rule
394	and path (those rows carry no subject identity); B non-selection is read from the embedded
395	baseline policy and ScopeDocument. The baseline artifact records per-rule knowledge, not a per-path extent. An entry whose first attributable change along B→E4 would rest on a `null`
396	value is `INDETERMINATE` with `current-absence-unknown` (unknown E4) or
397	`baseline-absence-unknown` (unknown B), never `CODE-FIXED`, `UNCHANGED` or `CODE-NET-NEW` by
398	default. A change already established between known values before the unknown value keeps its
399	classification, so a known `CODE-NET-NEW` still fails. Rule coverage, evidence and execution
400	deficiencies remain independent of this knowledge.
401	
402	**Indeterminate reason selection (closed).** An entry publishes exactly one
403	`indeterminateReason`, the first applicable in this order: (1) `pivot-reevaluation-unavailable`
404	when a changed axis's pivot presence is `null` (E0 for a changed detector map, E1 policy, E2
405	scope, E3 waivers), whether that pivot was not bound or was bound without presence knowledge,
406	including a correspondence barrier on that pivot; (2) the evidence axis, evaluated per declared
407	`evidenceUse` in declaration order: `required-evidence-unavailable`, then for a gating rule
408	`evidence-availability-changed` or `evidence-content-changed`; (3) the detector disposition's
409	own reason when its method is `indeterminate`; (4) `baseline-absence-unknown` when the first
410	attributable change rests on a `null` B; (5) `current-absence-unknown` when it rests on a `null`
411	E4. Whole-comparison reasons perform no comparison and emit no entries.
412	
413	**An unmatched baseline occurrence is not proven absence.** A baseline that retains an unmatched
414	occurrence of a rule on a path (for example a symbol whose detector projection was unavailable)
415	does not prove that a fingerprint of that rule on that path was absent. A fingerprint present
416	only on a pivot stays in the comparison universe, the baseline's gating unmatched obligation
417	remains a `correspondence-incomplete` deficiency, and the entry is `INDETERMINATE`
418	(`baseline-absence-unknown`), not `CODE-NET-NEW`. A genuinely complete baseline that selects the
419	path, records complete absence knowledge and retains no such unmatched occurrence proves
420	`B=false`: a fingerprint present on a bound E1 pivot and hidden by disabling the rule in current is
421	`CODE-NET-NEW` with `subsequentDeltas=[policy]` and still gates (`code-net-new-policy-hidden`).
422	
423	E1–E3 preserve current non-substituted inputs: selected source, configuration,
424	provider/toolchain contexts, imports, native facts and Coverage, subject
425	inventories, attribution/search records and candidate-producer evidence.
426	Plan-bound envelopes are compared by their retained semantic contents after
427	removing only the explicitly substituted parent locators. A policy, scope or
428	waiver remint cannot authorize replacement of native evidence. E0 uses the
429	prior detector and its admitted dependencies over current source and can
430	therefore have different native contexts and evidence. Snapshot membership
431	alone is not proof that native extraction examined a path; a counterfactual
432	requiring evidence outside the attested extraction extent is unavailable.
433	
434	**Detector union.** Comparison covers the union of baseline and current detectors.
435	Added detectors set E0 false. Removed detectors require the actual current-trusted
436	prior detector pivot and set E1–E4 false; E0 must never be substituted with B.
437	Consequently a new bug hidden by removing its detector remains CODE-NET-NEW and
438	can gate. Missing prior execution is indeterminate, including detector removal.
439	
440	**Evidence axis.** Compare the exact bound `import2` identity sets per kind, with
441	payload/correspondence/scope/observation digests retained in each BoundImport.
442	Replacing an artifact with another of the same kind is still an evidence change
443	(`evidence-content-changed`). For a rule with declared `evidenceUse`: if required evidence is
444	absent on the current side the entry is `INDETERMINATE`
445	(`required-evidence-unavailable`) and the rule's coverage is unsatisfied; if
446	availability changed and the rule gates on either side, attribution is
447	`INDETERMINATE` (`evidence-availability-changed`); only for a non-gating rule may a
448	presence change be `EVIDENCE-DELTA`. Required evidence loss can never disappear as a
449	non-gating delta.
450	
451	**Audit profiles select gate semantics explicitly** (schema `AuditProfile`):
452	
453	| Profile | Gates CODE-NET-NEW | Gates newly live via policy/scope/waiver | Gates all current live | New waiver suppresses net-new | Rule gating under |
454	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
455	| `code-regression` (default for `audit`) | yes | no | no | no | baseline or current |
456	| `policy-change` | yes | yes | no | no | baseline or current |
457	| `full-current` | yes | yes | yes | yes | current only |
458	| `report-only` | no | no | no | yes | current only |
459	
460	A `CODE-NET-NEW` entry that is not live in current (hidden by a later detector, policy or scope
461	change, or by a waiver added in the same change; `subsequentDeltas` names the later axes) still gates under
462	`baseline-or-current` with `gateReason=code-net-new-policy-hidden`; that existing reason covers every
463	later hiding axis. Verdict is `fail`
464	if any entry gates, else `indeterminate` if any `INDETERMINATE` entry belongs to a
465	gating rule or a current gating rule has unsatisfied/unknown required Coverage or
466	evidence, else `pass`. Rule deficiencies are enumerated independently of findings;
467	zero emitted findings never establish complete analysis. Whole-comparison indeterminacy (unmapped project,
468	unsupported schema/recipe major, context document mismatch) performs no comparison
469	and emits zero entries with a typed remedy. Enum precedence never decides a gate.

473	## 4. Imported evidence: one wrapper, typed payloads (AR-11)
474	
475	There is exactly one import identity: `importId = 'import2:' + H('import', wrapper)`
476	where the wrapper is the foundation `import` descriptor (schemaVersion 2, kinds
477	`runtime|test|history|dependency|prepared`). Each kind admits exactly one canonical
478	payload domain. Native runtime/test/history formats are adapter inputs normalized
479	into the workflow-owned payload before wrapping.
480	
481	| Kind | Admitted payload domain | Owner |
482	|---|---|---|
483	| runtime | `workflow.import-payload.runtime.v1` | workflow |
484	| test | `workflow.import-payload.test.v1` | workflow |
485	| history | `workflow.import-payload.history.v1` | workflow |
486	| dependency | `native.import-payload.dependency-source.v1` | native |
487	| prepared | `native.import-payload.prepared-output.v1` | native |
488	
489	The closed registry names the exact schema document and JSON selector. Its
490	`payloadSchemaDigest` is raw SHA-256 of the entire schema document's bytes;
491	`payloadDigest` is raw SHA-256 of the canonical validated payload. The host validates
492	the selected payload, source correspondence, foundation scope descriptor,
493	BuildIdentityV1, ImportObservationV1 and wrapper using the trusted local schema
494	closure. Merely carrying a recognized payloadDomain is insufficient. Caller-supplied
495	schema bytes must equal the registry document exactly. No network schema resolution
496	is allowed. All auxiliary digests are raw SHA-256 of their canonical closed records;
497	those preimages are retained. The `import2` wrapper alone uses the H-domain recipe.
498	The same payload with different provenance or observation semantics is a different import.
499	
500	Any other pairing is `IMPORT.KIND_PAYLOAD_MISMATCH`; an unregistered payload schema is
501	`IMPORT.PAYLOAD_SCHEMA_UNREGISTERED`; no artifact-supplied schema is ever admitted.
502	`opensip import KIND PATH` is a mutation step with an import receipt; the user-named
503	PATH is a `UserInputPath` opened through the security unit's nofollow custody and
504	never enters identity; every path inside a payload is a strict `LogicalPath`.
505	
506	Source correspondence is mandatory (`IMPORT.MAPPING_REQUIRED`, `CONFIG.INVALID`):
507	the shared closed SourceCorrespondence union in common.schema.json,
508	`exact-snapshot` or `vcs-revision` with VCS/build/mapping fields. Staleness
509	against a Plan is a closed table (`StalenessRule`): snapshot-equal → `current`,
510	consumable; snapshot-differs / commit-differs → `stale`, unmapped-only;
511	commit-equal-dirty → `unverifiable`, unmapped-only; build-identity-differs →
512	`wrong-build`, unmapped-only. An equal clean commit is consumable only with an
513	admitted SourceMappingV1 whose source paths and hashes join the current snapshot
514	inventory; an equal commit without that mapping remains unmapped-only. Corrupt bytes → refused (`IMPORT.ARTIFACT_CORRUPT`).
515	Explicitly selecting a stale import for a Plan is `REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED`
516	with `IMPORT.STALE_FOR_PLAN` (2). Unmapped-only evidence may be listed and queried
517	but never feeds a predicate.
518	
519	**No-hits is not non-use.** Runtime subjects carry `observed-hit`,
520	`observable-unhit`, `unobservable` or `unmapped`. `observed-hit` supplies positive
521	execution evidence and `observable-unhit` supplies bounded negative evidence,
522	always together with the observation window and population; `unobservable`/`unmapped` never become unhit signals and the schema
523	refuses a hit count on them. One window never establishes universal non-use;
524	runtime coverage is never OpenSIP Coverage. History payloads are advisory priority
525	inputs unless a policy predicate explicitly declares `evidenceUse` for them.
526	
527	**A repair evidence requirement over one of these two relations has its own
528	owning outcome law**, `imported-evidence.schema.json#/x-opensip-imported-requirement-law`
529	(§6). It is separate from native §4.6 because these relations mint no `fact2` and
530	carry no Coverage, and **each kind is projected through its own payload**: a
531	runtime requirement reads `observability`, `observationWindow` and
532	`observedPopulation`; a history requirement reads `revisionRange` and
533	`collectionScope`, which are its bounds fields; `HistoryPayloadV1` also carries
534	subjects and has no runtime observation-window, population or observability
535	fields. Neither kind may report the other's outcomes.
536	
537	**A repair target is a fingerprint, not a path, and the join is published.**
538	`RepairPlanDescriptor.targets` are `finding-key2:` **fingerprints**, while
539	`RuntimeSubject` is keyed by `{path, symbol?}` and `HistorySubject` by `{path}`.
540	The deterministic projection is
541	`imported-evidence.schema.json#/x-opensip-imported-requirement-law/targetSubjectProjection`:
542	each target must be a finding of the evidence Run named by `evidenceRunId` (preview
543	already refuses one that is not); that `finding-key2` identity is the H identity of
544	the retained foundation `finding-fingerprint` descriptor, whose retention is
545	`preimage` and whose bytes are therefore re-hashed at Run closure; and its
546	`subjectKey` supplies the path and qualified name used for matching. The projection
547	does not classify the target by `kind`, whose vocabulary is not closed here. A
548	runtime row matches on path and, if it names a symbol, on qualified name; another
549	symbol's row does not match. A runtime row with no symbol and every history row
550	provide **file** granularity, with `granularityWidenedToFile` disclosed in the
551	projection and successful outcome. A symbol-naming runtime row provides the
552	format's path-and-name granularity, not an exact match of the whole subject key:
553	neither format distinguishes `language`, `kind` or `discriminator`. Distinct
554	findings can therefore project to the same observation. This stated limit applies
555	to every such projection; it cannot establish execution or non-execution of a
556	particular subject variant beyond the captured granularity. More than one
557	matching subject **refuses**: an ambiguous projection is not resolved by choosing
558	one. A target with no matching subject is unsupported — never satisfied, and never
559	read as evidence of non-use.
560	
561	Five limits carry over and are enforced rather than assumed.
562	**Satisfied does not mean positive**: `observed-hit` is positive execution
563	evidence and `observable-unhit` is *bounded negative* evidence, both can satisfy,
564	and the disclosure records which did. **No imported observation establishes a
565	universal negative** — one window is not universal non-use — and imported evidence
566	can never *by itself* establish the native closed world or authorize an unsafe
567	`delete`/`replace`, and it can never **improve** that gate either: the gate reads
568	only the **native** `ClosedWorldV2` records the §6 relevance rule selects from the
569	evidence Run, and no imported observation is one of them.
570	It may still be an **additional required condition** alongside an
571	already-established native basis, so it is wrong to say it never affects
572	applicability; an unsatisfied imported requirement makes an otherwise-eligible
573	plan inapplicable. **Whole-versus-partial** is decided by the requirement's
574	`completeness` field: `complete` needs every plan target supported,
575	`partial-acceptable` at least one. That enum already existed, but **this reading of
576	it for an imported requirement over plan targets is selected here** and was not
577	previously published. A target that is unobservable or outside the history
578	collection scope therefore only names the cause *more precisely when the support
579	test fails* — it does not veto a lawful `partial-acceptable` requirement that has a
580	supported target. **Bounds are separate from support**: an insufficient observation
581	window or revision range applies under both completeness values, because it is a
582	property of the observation rather than of the target count. And **required versus
583	optional** stays where `evidenceUse` puts it — an optional absence remains the
584	`IMPORT.ABSENT_FOR_PREDICATE` disclosure and is satisfied *by absence* rather than
585	by evidence. That declaration reaches the requirement boundary as a **typed
586	boolean**; a non-boolean refuses, so there is no `unknown` state to default and no
587	falsy value is read as optional.

872	  carries no such wire field and none is claimed.
873	
874	The two vocabularies are **disjoint**, and a cross-plane value — a native
875	requirement claiming `import-unmapped-only`, or an imported one claiming
876	`resolution-incomplete` — is refused at admission, as is an outcome of the wrong
877	imported **kind**, such as a history range cause on a runtime relation. This schema
878	**deliberately leaves the authoritative registry lookup to admission**: it admits
879	either vocabulary and does not attempt to reproduce the relation registries, which
880	it could not fetch rows from in any case. That is a design choice about where the
881	authority lives, not a limitation of JSON Schema — a schema *can* branch on a
882	property's `const`/`enum` even where the base type is a broader string — and
883	duplicating a registry as schema conditionals would create exactly the drift this
884	contract set avoids elsewhere. The division is stated rather than implied.
885	
886	The value carried is the **satisfaction/deficiency projection** of its producer's
887	result, not that result: `sufficiency_v2` also returns `causes` on both branches
888	and may return `disclosures` on a failing branch. Those are producer result arrays
889	and are fields of no retained record; what is retained is the evidence the
890	evaluation read, so the projection drops nothing that was retained. Presence is **typed**: `deficiency` is **required
891	exactly when `satisfied` is false** and **forbidden when it is true**, `satisfied`
892	must be an actual boolean, and an explicit `null` is refused in both branches
893	because a present key with a null value is not an absent key. Both boundaries — the
894	schema and the preview admission — decide that same law and are held equal on an
895	enumerated shape table. The field previously named
896	`D9Deficiency`, which cannot express four of the nine outcomes its only producer
897	emits — `derivation-policy-unmet`, `external-consumers-unknown`,
898	`input-closure-incomplete` and `resolution-incomplete` — leaving three conforming
899	readings and no document choosing between them: write the D9-mapped value, which

900	is `verdict-indeterminate` for **all four** and so cannot tell
901	`resolution-incomplete` (the outcome §4.6 step 6 mandates for a universal
902	negative under `unresolvedEdgePolicy=forbid` over an affected target, and the one
903	a destructive unused-code recipe turns on) from three unrelated causes; write the
904	sufficiency value and be schema-invalid; or omit the field and drop the
905	disclosure. Retyping this one per-requirement field is the correction.
906	`D9Deficiency` is **unchanged** and still carries every whole-Run and
907	comparison-step termination — three of its members name evaluation, baseline and
908	query outcomes no per-requirement evaluation can produce — and the public D9
909	route for a Run carrying such a requirement is still native §10's. The value is a
910	**disclosure, not an authorization**: `applicable` is false whenever any
911	requirement is unsatisfied, the exact cause is carried into that requirement's
912	unmet precondition so two different causes are two different remedies, the
913	evidence authority remains the sealed Run named by `evidenceRunId`, and any edit
914	to the value mints a different `repairPlanId` that no authorization names.
915	That unmet precondition is emitted once per unsatisfied requirement and carries
916	the existing `REPAIR.EVIDENCE_RUN_UNAVAILABLE` code, which here says that the
917	evidence Run cannot supply what this repair requires and asserts nothing about the
918	Run having been purged or lost — `evidence.purged` and `evidence.missing` keep
919	their own distinct meaning in query results. Preview therefore reaches that one
920	code by two routes, the retained-availability and replayable-assurance failure of
921	the first paragraph above and this per-requirement insufficiency, and the remedy
922	is what tells them apart: the retention entry's remedy names the Run-level
923	restoration that route needs, while the per-requirement entry's remedy names that
924	requirement's `relation`, `minResolution`, evidence plane and exact `deficiency`.
925	`EvidenceRequirement.deficiency` remains the typed cause carrier: no
926	per-deficiency detail code is minted, because the closed public registry is not
927	where a per-requirement outcome vocabulary belongs. An unsatisfied requirement
928	with an empty `unmetPreconditions` is **not** a conforming projection — the schema
929	alone admits that shape, and the emission is decided at admission, the same
930	division of labour already stated for the deficiency vocabulary.
931	
932	`RepairPlanDescriptor.closedWorld` is a deterministic **five-field display
933	summary** of the selected records — `deadCodeRepairEligible`, `exportsClosed`,
934	`entryPointsRecognized`, `nonliteralLoading`, `externalConsumers` — and
935	`repair.schema.json` closes it at exactly those five, so a literal copy of
936	`ClosedWorldV2`, which carries seven, is refused there. It is **not** a native
937	producer record and does not claim to be one: a fieldwise reduction over several
938	entries may combine members that no single producer emitted together. That is
939	acceptable only because the record carries **no authority**. The reduction is
940	total and fixed:
941	
942	* `deadCodeRepairEligible` is the conjunction over the selected records, and
943	  `false` when none were selected.
944	* each remaining member takes the **least-closed** value present, ordering
945	  `closed ≺ open ≺ unknown`, `all ≺ partial ≺ none`, `none ≺ present`,
946	  `none-declared ≺ possible ≺ unknown`.
947	* **absence is folded in, not hidden.** When any relevant universe retains no
948	  native Coverage, or any selected binding's ownership of an unsafe path is
949	  unresolved, the reduction additionally folds in the sentinel below, so the
950	  summary cannot read as closed while eligibility is refused for that absence.
951	
952	With nothing selected the same rule yields the **five-field least-closed display
953	sentinel**, which is exactly
954	`{deadCodeRepairEligible: false, exportsClosed: unknown, entryPointsRecognized:
955	none, nonliteralLoading: present, externalConsumers: unknown}`. It is **not an
956	"all-unknown" record** and must not be described as one: only two members are
957	`unknown`; the other three are a false boolean and the least-closed pole of each
958	of the two enums that cannot spell absence. `ClosedWorldV2` has no `unknown`
959	member for `entryPointsRecognized` (`all|partial|none`) or `nonliteralLoading`
960	(`none|present`), so their poles stand in. That is this display rule applied
961	uniformly — **not** an observation that entry points went unrecognised or that
962	nonliteral loading was seen — and widening the native enum is not this section's
963	to do.
964	
965	**The summary grants no evidence authority of its own.** **No member of it is
966	authoritative, the boolean included**; the authority is the full native selection
967	above. It is never an input to
968	the gate, which reads the full selected records including the two members the
969	summary does not carry. No edit to it can make a plan applicable, since the whole
970	descriptor is the preimage of `repairPlanId`
971	(`H('workflow.repair-plan', descriptor)`) and apply requires a security
972	authorization bound to that exact `repairPlanId`, base snapshot and project.
973	Preview is a Query-class step and is **not** authorization: `applicable=true` is
974	a disclosure that the preconditions held, and trust, consent, current-snapshot
975	equality and that bound authorization are all still required at apply.
976	
977	**Create-only plans still carry a summary.** A plan with no `delete` and no
978	`replace` activates no gate, and an ineligible closed world alone adds **no**
979	unmet precondition to it. It still **reads** the selection and still **builds**
980	the five-field member — the member is `required` in the descriptor and the whole
981	descriptor is the `repairPlanId` preimage, so a create-only plan does not escape
982	the question, it only escapes the veto. It is summarised by the same reduction,
983	falling back to the **five-field least-closed sentinel above** — not an
984	all-unknown record — when the Run retains no relevant native Coverage at all, so
985	the descriptor, and therefore `repairPlanId`, is deterministic for a create-only
986	plan exactly as for any other.
987	
988	**What this changes, stated precisely.** The identity *recipe* and the descriptor
989	*shape* are unchanged: the same five member names, the same `additionalProperties:
990	false`, the same schema majors, and `repairPlanId` is still
991	`H('workflow.repair-plan', descriptor)` over the whole descriptor. What moves is
992	the *value* this member takes, so an implementation that previously used a
993	caller-selected record may now mint a different `repairPlanId` for the same
994	request. **No equality of `repairPlanId` is claimed across different Runs**:
995	`evidenceRunId` is part of the preimage, so a different Run is a different plan
996	identity however similar its evidence. Equality holds only where every descriptor
997	input, that Run included, is identical.
998	
999	The authority stays the sealed Run named by `evidenceRunId`. No claim is made here
1000	that a later step re-reads it — `repair verify` seals a **new** Run over the
1001	freshly re-snapshotted tree (`appliedSnapshotId` → `verifiedSnapshotId`) and
1002	compares remaining and net-new findings; it does not re-open the original evidence
1003	Run.
1004	
1005	**Apply** (`repair-apply`, mutation) is bound to the exact `repairPlanId`, base
1006	snapshot and project by a security-unit authorization (`REPAIR.CONSENT_NOT_BOUND`);
1007	CI requires policy consent. Current recipe trust and live authorization are checked
1008	again immediately before apply. It journals `RepairApplyJournalV1` through
1009	`PREPARING → STAGED → APPLYING → APPLIED → COMMITTED`: every postimage is written to a
1010	same-directory temp and digest-verified, every preimage is re-verified against the
1011	live file (`REPAIR.TARGET_PREIMAGE_MISMATCH` leaves `FAILED_CLEAN`), renames proceed in
1012	ascending path order, then the tree is re-snapshotted (`appliedSnapshotId`) and the
1013	receipt written. A fault during `APPLYING` restores every renamed target
1014	(`FAILED_ROLLED_BACK`, rollback `completed`); a renamed target that is neither
1015	preimage nor postimage is `RECOVERY_BLOCKED` with the paths listed and no automatic
1016	action. Replaying apply with the same idempotency key returns the completed receipt
1017	with a new replay delivery receipt and `replayed=true`; the original is preserved.
1018	
1019	**Recover** (`repair-recover`) is a closed table over journal state: PREPARING/STAGED
1020	→ discard temps (`FAILED_CLEAN`); APPLYING → roll back renamed (`FAILED_ROLLED_BACK`)
1021	or block if a target is unrecognized; APPLIED/INDETERMINATE → verify every exact
1022	postimage and the complete applied-path set before re-snapshot and commit;
1023	COMMITTED/FAILED_* → none; RECOVERY_BLOCKED → refuse (`HOST.IO_FAILURE`,
1024	`REPAIR.RECOVERY_BLOCKED`, exit 4). Every recovery mutation requires an authorization
1025	bound to this repairPlanId and journal requestId; inspection alone is read-only.
1026	Restore verifies all available retained preimage hashes before its first write.
1027	Corrupt bytes yield LEDGER.CORRUPT / REPAIR.PREIMAGE_CORRUPT (4) with no target change.
1028	Unavailable bytes return an exact restore intent and REPAIR.RECOVERY_REQUIRES_BROKER,
1029	without claiming rollback completed. Recovery never re-applies an edit.
1030	
1031	**Verify** (`verify`) always admits a **fresh snapshot** after apply; it never reuses
1032	the pre-apply Run. If the fresh snapshot differs from `appliedSnapshotId` the step is
1033	`REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED` / `REPAIR.SOURCE_MOVED` and no Run is sealed; otherwise
1034	it seals a new authoritative Run and reports `VerificationOutcome`
1035	(applied/verified snapshot, targets remaining, net-new findings). A separate immutable VerificationLinkV1 binds receiptId, verificationRunId, both
1036	snapshots and the verification request/step. The apply receipt is never rewritten
1037	and remains retained if verification fails.

1041	## 7. Explicitly authorized test execution (AR-08)
1042	
1043	Repository code execution is disabled by default. `opensip test run` (request class
1044	`execution`) is admitted only when: the security unit admits a `RepoExecutionGrantV2`
1045	with principal `P-TRUSTED-REPO`, execution class `test-runner`, bound to this
1046	project, snapshot digest and the exact `argv` digest, expiry operation-end, never
1047	inherited (`TEST.PRINCIPAL_NOT_ADMITTED` otherwise); CI uses a pre-existing policy
1048	record (`TEST.INTERACTIVE_CONSENT_IN_CI`); `argv[0]` is a `LogicalPath` member of the
1049	sealed snapshot or a member of the declared toolchain `closure2`
1050	(`TEST.ARGV_NOT_IN_CLOSURE`); the working directory is the project root or a
1051	`LogicalPath` inside it; the environment is constructed from an allowlist only, `PATH`
1052	is never copied (`TEST.ENV_NOT_ALLOWLISTED`) and is set to the toolchain closure; and
1053	the live tree still equals the `afterStep` snapshot. There is no shell string and no
1054	interpolation anywhere in the schema.
1055	
1056	**Argv digest.** `argvDigest` is the lowercase hexadecimal raw SHA-256 of `C(argv)`, where
1057	`C` is product canonical JSON (identity-and-evidence §3) and `argv` is the exact ordered array
1058	of argument strings actually selected for the spawn. Every element stays a separate array
1059	member, preserving order, repeated elements and any empty string an owning schema admits; no
1060	shell-joined, quoted, normalized or PATH-resolved surrogate is digested. The recipe is the same
1061	wherever the digest binds, `RepoExecutionGrantV2.argvDigest` (security S10) and
1062	`TestPayloadV1.argvDigest`: host test execution digests `TestExecutionStepParams.argv`, native
1063	preparation digests the host-selected preparation argv of its grant, and an independently
1064	prepared test payload digests the argument array its adapter recorded.
1065	
1066	The step **discloses** and does not confine: `effects.network/subprocess/
1067	filesystemWrite` are `DISCLOSURE-ONLY` unless the security unit's platform truth
1068	table measures a primitive; a claimed enforcement without a measured primitive is
1069	refused (`TEST.CONFINEMENT_CLAIM_REFUSED`). Every effect value must equal the selected
1070	truth-table profile row (security S10). The selected `permission-truth-tables.v9` profile has
1071	no measured platform-primitive row, so `ENFORCED-PLATFORM:<primitiveId>` cannot be claimed in
1072	this profile and is not a member of `TestExecutionStepParams` `EnforcementValue`; security
1073	`EnforcementV1` keeps that vocabulary for a future measured primitive, which requires a
1074	successor truth-table profile and test-execution schema. The mandatory sentence before spawn is
1075	"Repository test command will run with your user authority. OpenSIP does not prevent
1076	network access or other effects on this platform." Output is bounded and truncation
1077	is recorded. The outcome is a `TestPayloadV1` wrapped as an `import2` of kind `test`
1078	— evidence, never Coverage and never a verdict; a verdict may depend on it only
1079	through a declared policy predicate. Imported independently prepared test results
1080	are the supported alternative.

1085	
1086	`workflows/command-inventory.v3.json` is the single intended inventory,
1087	validated by `workflows/schemas/evaluator3/command-inventory.schema.json`; the checker refuses a command name
1088	outside the closed enum and requires every golden to be reachable by the model.
1089	
1090	| Group | Commands |
1091	|---|---|
1092	| analysis | `opensip` (default: discovery + durable analyze), `analyze [--ephemeral] [--baseline]`, `fit` (advisory whole-repository report), `audit --baseline [--audit-profile] [--closure-bundle]`, `repair verify` |
1093	| query | `recommend` (advisory next-step suggestions from discovery), `query OP`, `baseline show`, `policy show`, `policy test`, `candidates`, `inspect`, `review brief`, `repair preview` |
